items.title: ‘Nigeria dodged a massive howitzer,’ Keyamo slams Obi over public funds comment
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, over his claim that Nigeria could be wealthier if public funds were kept in banks to earn interest. Reacting in a post on his X account on Wednesday, Keyamo described Obi’s remarks as unintelligent and linked them to what he claimed was a decline in the former governor’s approval ratings. “This dumbness is beyond measure. I really don’t know whether to laugh or to cry. No wonder his approval ratings have plummeted so badly. “Nigeria did not just dodge a bullet; it ducked a massive howitzer!” Keyamo wrote. Vanguard had reported that Obi, speaking during an interview with a radio station in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, argued that Nigeria would be significantly wealthier if leaders left public funds in banks to generate interest instead of mismanaging the country’s resources. “I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank; they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said Obi also addressed questions surrounding his administration’s public engagements, explaining that he believed the results of government projects should speak for themselves because they were financed with public funds. “We did what we were doing with public money, so the public already see us working, so why are we going to do the ceremony or showing it on TV? Maybe I was wrong, but that was what happened,” he said. The post ‘Nigeria dodged a massive howitzer,’ Keyamo slams Obi over public funds comment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kankan : Un tradi-praticien retrouvé sans vie dans son véhicule au quartier Mbalia Frakono
items.description: La soirée de ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026, a été marquée par une découverte macabre dans le quartier Mbalia Frakono. Un père de famille, Ibrahima Baba Sangaré, tradi-praticien de son état, a été retrouvé inconscient à l'intérieur de son véhicule de marque Toyota, immatriculé BB 8804. Selon les premiers témoignages recueillis sur les lieux, la victime serait arrivée au volant de sa voiture avant de se garer. « C'est un monsieur qui est venu dans son véhicule se garer et se mettre à l'aise. Il est monté dans son véhicule, mais comme les riverains ont constaté que la voiture ne bougeait pas pendant un long moment, ils se sont rapprochés pour trouver l'homme couché à l'intérieur », a rapporté le Commissaire adjoint Sekou Mariama Sagno, du Commissariat central de Kankan. Alertées, les forces de l'ordre se sont rendues sur place pour prendre les dispositions nécessaires. « L'information a été remontée à la police. Nous avons pris les dispositions pour que le monsieur soit transporté à l'hôpital régional de Kankan, sous l'autorisation du procureur. Nous sommes là pour la sécurisation des lieux », a précisé le Commissaire adjoint Sagno. Interrogé sur l'état de santé de la victime au moment de la découverte, le représentant des forces de l'ordre est resté prudent : « Pour le moment, on ne peut pas dire qu'il est mort ou pas. » Cependant, une source au sein de l'hôpital régional de Kankan, où l'homme a été évacué, a confirmé son décès peu après son admission. La victime, âgée d'environ 70 ans, était mariée à une femme et père de neuf enfants. Les circonstances exactes de ce drame restent, pour l'heure, inconnues.

items.title: ‘‘Le ragazze di Tunisi’’ de Luca Bianchini | Une lumineuse saga familiale
items.description: Dans son roman ‘‘Le ragazze di Tunisi’’ (Les filles de Tunis) (édité par Mondadori, Milan, 19 février 2026, 264 pages), Luca Bianchini dresse, avec son style inimitable, un portrait saisissant de liens indéfectibles et d’espoirs qui résistent au temps. Il évoque une émigration presque oubliée, celle des Siciliens partis chercher fortune dans une Tunisie cosmopolite et vibrante, alors sous protectorat français, et ce à travers le destin de la famille Brancata. Latif Belhedi Dans ‘‘Le ragazze di Tunisi ’’, Luca Bianchini nous offre une saga familiale lumineuse et mélancolique, où, dans les années 1959-1961, Maria, une couturière courageuse, élève ses trois filles adolescentes entre les épreuves du quotidien et les rêves d’un avenir meilleur. Sur fond d’une ville, Tunis, suspendue entre le charme du passé et le souffle de l’indépendance, s’entremêlent premiers amours, chansons de Mina à la radio et l’approche inéluctable des adieux. Avec son style inimitable, Luca Bianchini dresse un portrait saisissant de liens indéfectibles et d’espoirs qui résistent au temps. Qui était Maria ? Était-elle sicilienne ? Italienne ? Française ? En réalité, elle se sentait avant tout une fille de Tunis. «Je ne connaissais pas vraiment l’histoire de la famille de ma mère, jusqu’au jour où j’ai commencé à poser des questions» , raconte Luca Bianchini. Dans le quartier du Borgel Les Brancata du roman de Bianchini font partie de ces nombreuses familles d’origine sicilienne qui, en Tunisie, ont cherché «l’Amérique» — sans toujours la trouver. En revanche, elles ont vécu en bonne intelligence avec les Français — qui, jusqu’alors, détenaient le pouvoir —, ainsi qu’avec les Tunisiens, les Juifs et les Maltais. Dans ce cadre cosmopolite, Maria — une belle femme de trente-huit ans, fière et déterminée — voit ses trois filles adolescentes grandir. C’est elle qui s’occupe d’elles, car son mari travaille à la campagne ; elle se retrouve donc presque toujours seule. Pour faire face aux difficultés économiques, elle réalise de petits travaux de couture chez elle, dans le quartier du Borgel, au rez-de-chaussée d’un immeuble donnant sur une cour où tout le monde se connaît. À l’étage, un veuf taciturne lui fait une cour discrète, mais Maria est trop absorbée par la surveillance de ses filles — en particulier Anna, l’aînée. À seize ans, Anna aime lire et observer les navires à l’horizon ; elle fréquente l’une des meilleures écoles de Tunis grâce à son oncle Jojo, le «voyou latin» de la famille, qui finance ses études. Pour elle, l’amour demeure encore quelque chose d’inaccessible, mais heureusement, elle peut compter sur Marinette, son amie française, qui lui ouvre les portes d’un univers fait de cinéma, de belles tenues et de promenades sur l’avenue de France. Autour d’elles gravitent sans cesse ses sœurs : Vitina, qui ne semble penser qu’au chant et à la gymnastique, et Pupetta, la «conscience» — ou le «grillon parlant» — de la famille. Un temps suspendu Tout autour, une ville animée où nos protagonistes évoluent dans un temps suspendu, entre mélancolie et incertitude : avec l’indépendance de la Tunisie, l’heure des adieux approche pour beaucoup. Mais c’est précisément la peur du changement qui enflamme les cœurs, fait naître de nouvelles histoires et révèle des secrets, au sein d’un microcosme peuplé d’oncles rancuniers, de voisins curieux, de couscous à volonté et de soirées palpitantes devant la télévision. ‘‘Les Filles de Tunis’’ est un roman haut en couleur, aussi émouvant que surprenant. Luca Bianchini mêle souvenirs familiaux et anecdotes hilarantes pour retracer une histoire partagée par de nombreux Italiens. Il aurait été dommage de ne pas la raconter. Luca Bianchini est né le 11 février 1970 à Turin. Il continue d’écrire dans sa cuisine, même s’il n’a toujours pas appris à faire des fritures aussi bien que sa mère. Depuis 2003, Mondadori a publié tous ses romans. L’article ‘‘Le ragazze di Tunisi’’ de Luca Bianchini | Une lumineuse saga familiale est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Pillion riding banned in KP's Bajaur for 10 days owing to security situation
items.description: BAJAUR: The district administration banned pillion riding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur for 10 days on Thursday by invoking Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) owing to the security situation. The notification for the restriction, issued by Deputy Commissioner (DC) Adnan Farid’s office, said the measure was taken in view of reports from intelligence agencies and the police department. Given the prevailing security situation and the possible use of motorcycles in terrorist activities, there was a need for immediate preventive measures, the notification added. It said the DC was “satisfied that are sufficient grounds to proceed under Section 144 of the CrPC as immediate preventive measure to ensure public safety, avert any untoward incident, maintain law and order situation and peace in the district”. The ban on pillion riding was imposed with immediate effect and would remain in place till Nov 7 unless the order was modified or withdrawn earlier. The notification said any person violating the order would be punished under Section 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Pakistan Penal Code. Earlier, the authorities imposed a 15-day ban on pillion riding in Bajaur on September 5, citing the security situation back then as well. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

items.title: Gombe @30: Yahaya seeks continuity ahead of 2027
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya of Gombe State has called for continuity in governance, political unity and sustained investment in critical sectors as the state marks 30 years of creation, saying its future must transcend the ambitions of any individual or political party. Yahaya, reflecting on the state’s three-decade journey, said the anniversary provided an opportunity to celebrate past achievements and assess how statehood had translated into improved living conditions, expanded opportunities and inclusive development. The governor, whose second term ends in 2027, urged political leaders, traditional rulers, religious institutions, youths and other stakeholders to approach the forthcoming political transition with responsibility, peace and commitment to the collective interest of the state. Speaking against the backdrop of the anniversary theme, “Reflecting on our History, Consolidating Progress, and Charting the Future,” Yahaya said successive generations must understand the state’s history, preserve developmental gains and build institutions capable of outlasting individual administrations. He also highlighted achievements recorded under his administration in education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, industrialisation, electricity, environmental protection, public service reform and grassroots development. Gombe State was created on October 1, 1996, by the late General Sani Abacha following years of agitation for greater political representation, accelerated development and governance closer to the people. Yahaya expressed gratitude to Abacha and the state’s founding fathers and mothers, saying their contributions laid the foundation on which successive administrations had built. “Thirty years ago, a dream that our people had carried for generations finally became a reality. It was the recognition of a longstanding aspiration for greater representation, accelerated development, political inclusion and a stronger voice within the Nigerian federation,” he said. He, however, noted that state creation alone did not guarantee development, stressing that its value lay in expanding opportunities, deepening inclusion, improving governance and enhancing citizens’ welfare. According to him, Gombe’s development cannot be credited to any single administration, political party or individual, describing governance as a relay in which each generation must advance the work of its predecessors. The governor paid tribute to the state’s pioneer military administrators, Group Captain Joseph Orji and Lieutenant Colonel Mohammed Inuwa Bawa, for establishing the machinery of government and laying the institutional foundations of the state. He also acknowledged the contributions of the late Alhaji Abubakar Habu Hashidu, the first democratically elected governor; Senator Mohammed Danjuma Goje; and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, whose administrations, he said, contributed to the expansion of infrastructure, institutions and development opportunities. Yahaya, who served as Commissioner for Finance and Economic Development under Goje, said successive administrations had operated under different circumstances but contributed to the state’s development. “When I took the oath of office on May 29, 2019, I made a simple commitment: to leave Gombe better than I found it,” he said. He said the commitment informed his administration’s 10-year development agenda, DEVAGOM, designed to promote people-centred governance through institutional reforms, strategic investments and inclusive development. Education: Over 2,000 classrooms constructed, renovated On education, Yahaya said his administration declared a state of emergency in the sector and embarked on extensive infrastructure development to improve access to quality learning. He disclosed that more than 2,000 classrooms had been constructed or renovated across more than 400 schools, while four mega colleges had been built and 1,000 teachers recruited. The administration also provided school improvement grants, while the Better Education Service Delivery for All programme, BESDA, was used to bring 350,000 out-of-school children back into the education system. He added that integrated Almajiri and Tsangaya schools had been established across the state’s 11 local government areas to expand access to education. At the tertiary level, Yahaya said two additional faculties had been established at Gombe State University, while increased subventions had strengthened tertiary institutions’ capacity to deliver teaching, research and innovation. He described the enactment of the Gombe State Education Trust Fund Law as a major step towards establishing a sustainable financing framework for the sector. According to him, education remains central to the state’s long-term prosperity, competitiveness and social development. Healthcare: GoHealth covers over 400,000 beneficiaries In the health sector, Yahaya said his administration had constructed or renovated 228 primary healthcare centres to provide two functional facilities in each of the state’s 114 political wards. He listed the construction of the General Hospital in Kumo, its subsequent conversion into a Federal Medical Centre, the renovation of general hospitals in Bajoga and Kaltungo, and the upgrading of the Gombe State Specialist Hospital among the interventions recorded under his administration. The governor said the establishment of the Hospitals Management Board was intended to improve healthcare administration, while the GoHealth contributory healthcare scheme had expanded access to medical services. According to him, the scheme now covers more than 400,000 beneficiaries, including approximately 100,000 poor and vulnerable citizens. He added that 440 healthcare professionals had been recruited and the CONMESS and CONHESS salary structures implemented to improve remuneration for health workers. Yahaya said the measures reflected his administration’s commitment to making healthcare more accessible, particularly to rural communities and vulnerable populations. Infrastructure, urban renewal and housing On infrastructure, the governor said the Network 11-100 initiative had facilitated the construction and rehabilitation of more than 1,000 kilometres of roads across the state, with several roads complemented by solar-powered streetlights. He listed the Gombe City Centre Underpass and the Gombe Northern Bypass among the major projects undertaken to improve mobility, connect communities, enhance public safety and stimulate economic activity. The administration, he said, also established the Gombe Geographic Information Systems (GOGIS) and reformed the Gombe State Urban Planning and Development Authority (GOSUPDA) to strengthen land administration, physical planning and urban development. Yahaya disclosed that work had commenced on a Three-Arms Zone comprising the State House of Assembly Complex, State High Court Complex and State Secretariat. He said the government had also constructed 550 housing units through the Family Homes Funds and another 500 in collaboration with the North-East Development Commission. According to him, the investments were intended to strengthen democratic institutions, improve public administration and provide housing opportunities for residents. Industrialisation, agriculture and investment In agriculture and industrialisation, Yahaya said the government was working to harness Gombe’s economic advantages by promoting productivity, value addition, enterprise development and private-sector investment. He identified the 1,000-hectare Muhammadu Buhari Industrial Park as a major investment in the state’s industrial future, providing a platform for manufacturing, entrepreneurship and employment generation. The ongoing Renewed Hope Agro-Industrial Hub, he said, was designed to position Gombe as a major centre for agricultural trading, processing and logistics in the North-East. The facility comprises an international livestock market, a modern grains market, an abattoir, an animal feeds market and an inland dry port. Yahaya attributed the state’s recognition as Nigeria’s leading state in ease of doing business in 2021 and 2022 to measures taken to improve the business environment, including the establishment of the Gombe State Investment Promotion Agency. He said the administration’s economic vision was to create an environment where government provides the necessary infrastructure and regulatory support, while businesses, farmers, entrepreneurs and investors drive growth and employment. Electricity and water supply The governor said his administration had taken advantage of opportunities created by the Electricity Act 2023 to strengthen the state’s electricity sector through the establishment of the Gombe State Electricity Regulatory Commission and the Gombe Electricity Company. He cited the completion of the one-megawatt Talasse solar mini-grid as a significant achievement, adding that similar projects in Filiya and Gelengu had reached about 90 per cent completion. According to him, additional mini-grid projects had been flagged off in Akko, Dukku, Funakaye and Kaltungo as part of a broader plan to connect 80 communities to an interconnected mini-grid network. On water supply, Yahaya said the expansion of the Gombe regional water distribution network and the provision of dedicated electricity for the Gombe water treatment plant were nearing completion. He expressed optimism that the projects would help address longstanding water shortages in Gombe and neighbouring communities. Environment, public service reforms and workers’ welfare On environmental protection, the governor said the Gombe Goes Green initiative had set a target of planting four million trees to combat desertification, restore degraded landscapes and strengthen environmental resilience. He also highlighted erosion-control interventions around the Federal College of Education, Mallam Inna, Gombe State University and Hayin Misau, saying the projects were intended to protect lives, homes, livelihoods and public infrastructure. In the public service, Yahaya said his administration had established the Bureau of Public Service Reforms, implemented the N70,000 minimum wage for state and local government employees, and carried out promotions and appointments across the civil service. He further disclosed that more than N44 billion had been paid in pension and gratuity obligations, including N21 billion inherited from the previous administration. At the grassroots, he said the government had strengthened local government financial discipline and administrative capacity while creating 13 Local Council Development Areas to bring governance closer to communities. On security, Yahaya said his administration had worked with security agencies, traditional institutions and local communities to sustain peace in the state. He listed the establishment of GOSTEC, the revitalisation of community-based dispute-resolution mechanisms and improved security coordination among the measures taken to strengthen public safety. He also reiterated his support for state police as part of broader efforts to reform Nigeria’s security architecture. Yahaya acknowledges challenges, seeks continuity Despite the achievements highlighted, Yahaya acknowledged that Gombe still faced significant developmental challenges, stressing that his administration did not consider every problem solved or every aspiration fulfilled. He said the gains recorded had been achieved amid national and global difficulties, including the COVID-19 pandemic, economic recessions, fiscal constraints and security challenges affecting the wider northern region. The governor attributed the state’s progress, despite the constraints, to the resilience of its people, the commitment of public servants and cooperation with development partners. Looking ahead, he said his vision was to bequeath a Gombe that was economically competitive, socially inclusive, environmentally resilient and institutionally strong. He envisaged a state where every child had access to quality education, young people acquired relevant skills, women realised their potential, healthcare was accessible, communities were secure and infrastructure served all parts of the state. He stressed the need for long-term planning, technological innovation, stronger private-sector partnerships and continuity in public policies to sustain development gains beyond his administration. “The future of Gombe State must always be greater than the ambitions of any individual or political party,” he said. Gombe at 30: Preserving history, preparing for 2027 As part of efforts to preserve the state’s history, Yahaya announced the preparation of a commemorative publication titled Gombe State: Thirty Years of Promise and Progress, 1996–2026. He described the book as an effort to document the struggle for state creation, the evolution of public institutions, the contributions of successive administrations, the state’s socioeconomic transformation and its future development prospects. The governor commended the editorial committee, researchers, contributors and other stakeholders involved in the project, saying the publication would provide a reference point for future scholarship, policymaking and public understanding. With the 2027 general elections approaching, Yahaya urged political stakeholders to place the collective interest of Gombe above partisan differences. He said the anniversary should remind residents that the movement for state creation had been sustained by a common purpose that transcended individual interests. “I therefore appeal to all our political leaders, traditional institutions, religious leaders, young people and citizens across the state to approach the coming transition with a spirit of peace, responsibility and shared commitment to our common future,” he said. Yahaya added that the greatest tribute to the state’s founding fathers and mothers would be to ensure that Gombe continued to fulfil the promise that inspired its creation. He concluded that while the first 30 years had been devoted to establishing the foundations of statehood and progress, the next three decades should focus on consolidating those gains and building a prosperous future for generations yet unborn. The governor also commended the Gombe State at 30 Planning Committee and Secretariat for organising the anniversary and thanked former governors, traditional and religious leaders, development partners, security agencies, delegations from other states and citizens at home and in the diaspora for their contributions to the state’s development. items.title: Afghanistan opium poppy cultivation surges despite Taliban govt ban: UN
items.description: Opium poppy cultivation in Afghanistan more than quadrupled in 2026 despite a Taliban government ban, the United Nations said on Thursday, urging that impoverished farmers needed alternatives to the lucrative crop. Cultivated areas reached 43,000 hectares (around 106,200 acres), up from 10,000 hectares in 2025, while estimated opium production jumped fivefold from 300 tonnes to 1,500 tonnes, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) said in a report. Long the world’s leading producer of poppies, Afghanistan was overtaken by Myanmar after a 2022 Taliban government ban crushed the trade in the country. But rampant poverty has driven some farmers to return to the trade. “Without opium, we cannot even afford basic food,” Mohammad, a 22-year-old farmer in Afghanistan’s northeast, told AFP. This photograph taken on June 22, 2026 shows Afghan farmers harvesting sap from poppies in a field in Badakhshan province. — AFP Afghanistan’s 2022 crackdown drove cultivated areas down from more than 200,000 hectares to 10,000 hectares in 2025. Myanmar cultivated 53,000 hectares in 2025, with no 2026 figures available. The Taliban authorities claim to have destroyed more than 22,000 hectares. But UNODC said many poppy plots were concealed among cereal crops or behind walls, making them difficult to detect. Mohammad lives with his parents in Badakhshan, which has become Afghanistan’s main opium poppy-growing province. “The Taliban threaten us and do not allow us to grow opium. We cultivate it with a great deal of fear,” he said, asking only to be identified by his first name. “I want to buy a car, build a house and get married. Without opium, I cannot achieve these things,” he further explained. ‘The only way’ In May, two people were killed in clashes that erupted as Afghan security forces moved to destroy opium poppy fields in Badakhshan. Another 35-year-old farmer named Mohammad, who ploughs his poppy field with an ox, said: “If we grow wheat, it is not enough to sustain our lives. We are forced to grow poppies to earn a good income.” Mohammad said that he is threatened by the authorities and sometimes his crops are destroyed, but he will continue. “It is the only way to cover living expenses,” he said. One hectare of wheat generated just over $770 in 2023, compared with $10,000 for a hectare of poppy, according to UNODC. This photograph taken on October 18, 2026 shows an Afghan farmer sowing poppy seeds in a field in Badakhshan province. — AFP “Opium prices slightly decreased from $570 per kilogramme in 2025 to $500 per kilogramme in 2026, remaining well above pre-ban levels of less than $100 per kilogramme,” UNODC said in a press release. “The fourfold increase in opium poppy cultivation shows the difficulty in sustaining decreases in illicit opium cultivation when poor farmers have no alternatives to feed their families,” said UNODC Executive Director Monica Juma. The Taliban government acknowledged that the ban was not a “sustainable and long-term solution” without alternative livelihoods and economic support for farmers. The challenge comes as Afghanistan faces the return of 6.6m Afghans since 2023, climate disasters, dwindling aid and banking isolation since the Taliban movement returned to power in 2021. With support from Japan and the European Union, UNODC has funded programmes to help farmers find alternatives. ‘International problem’ Through the NGO Afghan Aid, Zikrullah, 35, who supports an extended family of 12 in Badakhshan, received improved wheat seeds and fertiliser. “We’re satisfied, it takes less effort than opium and we’re more at ease,” he told AFP , also asking to be identified only by his first name. A third farmer named Mohammad, 30, who has converted 80 per cent of his land to wheat, told AFP that the lack of water in recent years has affected crops other than poppy. To curb opium production sustainably, alternative crops alone are insufficient, UNODC Country Representative for Afghanistan Polleak Ok Serei told AFP in an interview in Kabul. “Sustainable alternative livelihood requires more than thinking in terms of alternative crops,” he said. Farmers “need access to markets, including international markets through trades. They need infrastructure, roads, irrigation, storage”. UNODC estimated in 2025 that approach would require approximately $500m, but “only 10pc” had been funded by donors and the Taliban authorities, according to Ok Serei. The strategy also takes time, he said. “Thailand spent 15 years investing in alternative livelihood before starting eradicating,” Ok Serei said. The problem extends far beyond Afghanistan, he said. “It truly is an international problem,” Ok Serei added, explaining that Afghan drugs were consumed across other continents. Afghan opium is the main source of heroin in the European Union, where approximately 850,000 people used opioids in 2024, according to the European Union Drugs Agency. Addressing the problem requires international cooperation, the UN representative said. Ok Serei called for a “drug demand reduction strategy, not only in Afghanistan but also outside of Afghanistan”.

items.title: Judicial Reform: NBA’s unheeded proposal to restructure NJC
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri About two and a half years ago, precisely in April 2024, the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) proposed a bold reform to remove the Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, as the statutory chairman of the National Judicial Council, NJC. The NBA, as the umbrella body of legal practitioners in the country, faulted the composition of the Council, which is saddled with the responsibility of disciplining erring judicial officers. It not only challenged the current system, which mandates that the Council be headed by the CJN, but also demanded a review of its composition. According to the NBA: “The inherent flaws in the composition of the NJC impact negatively on its ability to prosecute judicial misconduct in a manner that inspires public confidence.” As part of its recommendations, the Bar proposed that the NJC be constituted as follows: six judicial officers appointed by the CJN; six lawyers nominated by the National Executive Council of the NBA, including the NBA President; and six non-lawyers appointed by the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, subject to Senate approval. “The Chairmanship of these bodies should be rotated between the heads of the three constituent groups,” the NBA insisted. Furthermore, the association recommended appointing court administrators to assume the administrative functions currently performed by the heads of court, including procurement, budgeting, court renovation, and the implementation of judicial appropriations. “These are activities within court administration that have severally been identified by the anti-corruption bodies as areas prone to corrupt activities. “This proposal for the creation of this office takes cognizance of the role of the Chief Registrars of courts who will under the proposed arrangements enable them (together with heads of courts) to concentrate solely on the business of adjudication especially case management without distraction.” The recommendations were contained in proposals the NBA submitted at a national summit on Justice Sector reforms. The Chairman of the Joint Planning Committee of the summit, Dr. Babatunde Ajibade, SAN, had, at that time, told newsmen that the reform proposals were considered and approved in modified form. “The general consensus reached by this panel was that the role of the NJC in discharging its responsibility for judicial appointments into the Superior Courts of Record required significant review. “There was a concern expressed about the fact that the CJN, who is the chairman of the NJC is also the chairman of the Federal Judicial Service Commission, which is the body that initially reviews proposals or lists of candidates for appointment into judicial office. “The members pointed out the seeming inconsistency between the CJN playing both those roles, as it would appear that he was then recommending candidates to himself being chairman of both bodies, and being the person who appoints a significant number of the members of both bodies other than those who are statutory members. “There was a general consensus that there was a need to reconstitute or propose the reconstitution of these bodies, both the NJC and the FJSC,” Ajibade, SAN, stated. However, years after the recommendations were made, both the NJC and the FJSC have remained structurally unchanged. The NJC was established under Section 153 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to safeguard the independence of the judiciary and ensure accountability in judicial administration. It was created as a replacement for the Advisory Judicial Committee (AJC), a legal body that operated during the military era, at a time when the judiciary had far less structural and administrative independence. With the return of the country to constitutional democracy, the NJC became the top judicial oversight organ, headed by the CJN, with its membership including the next most senior Justice of the Supreme Court; the President of the Court of Appeal; retired justices; various heads of courts; members of the NBA; and two non-lawyers of unquestionable integrity. Under the provisions of Paragraph 21 of Part One of the Third Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Council, among other things, recommends those to be appointed judges, as well as the removal from office of judicial officers found to have compromised standards in the discharge of their duties. The NJC makes such recommendations both to the President for judges under the Federal Judicial Service Commission (FJSC) and to Governors for judicial officers under the State Judicial Service Commissions. It is also the responsibility of the Council, through its committee, to periodically evaluate the performance of judges to ensure that the justice needs of citizens are duly met. Over the years, however, critics have called for a review of both the powers and composition of the NJC, citing its increasing failure to discharge its mandate effectively. A key area of concern is the judicial recruitment process, with critics arguing that unfit persons continue to be appointed, many of them either children of serving or retired judicial officers, or individuals loyal to people within the corridors of power. Critics insist that this has contributed to the poor quality of judicial decisions, often manifesting in conflicting judgments accompanied by allegations of bribery and corruption. The NJC is considered structurally weak: its members serve part-time, petitions are often decided at a snail’s pace, and sanctions feel token relative to the scale of corruption allegations. Notwithstanding the criticisms, the Council has periodically sacked or recommended the removal of judges for misconduct, and set up dedicated disciplinary machinery. In what appears to be the first major sweep to root out rotten eggs on the bench, the NJC, in a landmark resolution following its 111th meeting on May 13, 2026, queried 256 judges over various performance-related issues. It also suspended two High Court judges for one year without pay for misconduct and for breaching the right to a fair hearing. These developments followed renewed efforts by the CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, to cleanse the Augean stable. Justice Kekere-Ekun declared her zero tolerance for corruption when she appeared before the Senate for screening as the 23rd substantive CJN on September 25, 2024. True to her word, and in a clear departure from the old format, publication of the list of candidates shortlisted for appointment to the bench became mandatory. This paved the way for the public to blow the whistle on candidates with a deficit in their integrity quotient. Despite this initiative, calls for swifter action to guarantee accountability from the bench grew louder. It is not surprising that President Bola Tinubu had, in his 2023 manifesto, pledged to review the mandate and composition of the NJC. He said his administration would reposition the Council “to make it tougher and more effective in dealing with corruption, malpractice and incompetence in the administration of justice.” He had also proposed that the mandate of the NJC be limited to federal courts. However, more than three years into his administration, no changes have been made in either the composition or operations of the Council, even though President Tinubu himself has repeatedly acknowledged the need for reforms. He had, on November 17, 2025, urged the judiciary to take decisive action to address questions about its integrity, warning that justice must never be for sale. “Corruption in any arm of government weakens the nation, but corruption in the Judiciary destroys it at its core. “When justice is compromised, governance loses its integrity, and democracy loses its foundation,” President Tinubu stated as he flagged off the 2025 All Nigerian Judges Conference of the Superior Courts in Abuja. While acknowledging the concerns raised by President Tinubu, the CJN pledged action to restore public confidence in the judiciary. “On the persistent issue of corruption, we can no longer afford to regard our institution as beyond scrutiny. We must admit, with candour, that there are some within our ranks who have undermined the integrity of the Bench. This must change,” the CJN added. Although she did not attempt to conceal the rot within the judiciary, she warned against blanket allegations of corruption, insisting such claims be supported by evidence. The post Judicial Reform: NBA’s unheeded proposal to restructure NJC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ziguinchor : 28 individus interpellés lors d’une opération conjointe de la Gendarmerie et des Armées
items.description: Vingt-huit individus, dont neuf femmes, ont été interpellés à Ziguinchor lors d’une opération conjointe menée par la Gendarmerie nationale et les Armées, à la suite d’un rassemblement au cours duquel le drapeau du Mouvement des forces démocratiques de la Casamance (MFDC) a été hissé, selon un communiqué de la Gendarmerie. D’après la même source, cette opération s’inscrit dans le cadre des missions de préservation de l’ordre public et de protection de l’intégrité territoriale. Au cours de l’intervention, les forces de défense et de sécurité ont procédé au retrait du drapeau. Une perquisition a également permis de saisir plusieurs objets, notamment des téléphones portables, des documents et des insignes. Les vingt-huit personnes interpellées ainsi que les objets saisis ont été mis à la disposition de la Section de recherches de Ziguinchor pour les besoins de l’enquête, précise le communiqué.

items.title: Kalu opposes plenary invitation to INEC chairman
items.description: The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has opposed a proposal to invite the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, to brief the House on preparations for the 2027 general elections, arguing that the engagement could distract the commission. Kalu made the position known during Wednesday’s plenary while contributing to a motion jointly sponsored by the Minority Whip, Mansur Soro, and the Deputy Minority Leader, Abdulsamad Dasuki, seeking to invite the INEC chairman to address lawmakers on the commission’s preparations for the elections. Opposing the prayer seeking a plenary briefing, the deputy speaker argued that INEC’s recent public engagements were sufficient to address many of the concerns raised about the electoral process. He said further inquiries should be channelled through the House Committee on Electoral Matters, which has the mandate to interface with the commission on behalf of the legislature. According to Kalu, inviting the INEC chairman before the full House at this stage could create unnecessary pressure on the commission, trigger public anxiety and undermine confidence in the electoral process. He maintained that the commission had been engaging the public on its preparations and had not reported any logistical challenges. “I stand not in support of the prayer of this particular motion because supporting the prayer is belittling the mandate of the committee set up to carry out this function,” he said. Kalu questioned the need to summon Amupitan before the entire House shortly after his public briefing, urging lawmakers to have confidence in the relevant committees established to oversee the commission’s activities. “Inviting the chairman of INEC to come and brief the House when he just briefed the entire nation is not ideal. Don’t we believe in our committees again?” he asked. He proposed an amendment to the motion to require the INEC chairman to meet with the relevant committee rather than address the entire House at plenary. The deputy speaker also argued that the National Assembly, as an institution responsible for strengthening democracy, should support the electoral commission in carrying out its responsibilities rather than subjecting it to what he considered an ill-timed plenary inquiry. His proposed amendment was seconded by a member of the House, Babajimi Benson, who represents a constituency in Lagos State. When the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, put the motion to a voice vote, lawmakers overwhelmingly supported the amendment, after which he referred the matter to the House Committee on Electoral Matters. The committee is expected to handle the concerns raised in the motion and engage with INEC on its preparations for the 2027 general elections. items.title: US bans imports from Chinese genomics companies
items.description: The United States banned imports from three Chinese genomics companies on Wednesday over claims they collected genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities in China’s Xinjiang region. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said BGI Genomics, MGI Tech and Shenzhen BGI Technology, also known as BGI Group, had been added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List. The list identifies entities working with Xinjiang’s government “to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor or receive forced labor or Uyghurs, Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, or members of other persecuted groups out of Xinjiang.” The United Nations warned in 2022 of possible crimes against humanity in the region, including the detention of more than a million Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities in camps. China has repeatedly and vehemently denied accusations of human rights abuses against the Uyghurs. According to the US DHS, the companies “helped collect genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities, including people subjected to forced labor, meaning work they could not freely refuse.” Beijing said on Thursday that it “strongly condemns” Washington’s ban, which has “no factual basis”. “The US side continues to exploit the ‘human rights’ issue, using it as a pretext to pursue unilateral protectionism and bullying,” a commerce ministry spokesperson said in a statement. China urged the United States to “immediately cease its political manipulation and smear campaigns”, vowing to take necessary measures to safeguard its interests. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the United States refused to “let companies tied to forced labor and the surveillance of persecuted minorities profit from the American market.” BGI and MGI both denied the allegations, saying they oppose all forms of forced labour. The Trump administration proposed new rules last week to restrict investment in Chinese biotechnology companies. Other technologies already subject to scrutiny include artificial intelligence and computer chips — key frontiers in the ongoing economic competition between Beijing and Washington. AFP The post US bans imports from Chinese genomics companies appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Singapore foreign minister to undertake official visit to Pakistan on Oct 30
items.description: Singapore’s Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr Vivian Balakrishnan will undertake an official visit to Islamabad on Friday (Oct 30) at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday. “The visit assumes significance as it coincides with the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Singapore and comes ahead of Singapore’s assumption of the Asean chairmanship in 2027,” the FO said in a statement. During the visit, Dar and Dr Balakrishnan will hold bilateral talks covering the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Singapore relations and exchange views on regional and global developments of mutual interest, it added. A memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in disaster management between Pakistan’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Singapore’s Civil Defence Force (SCDF) will also be exchanged. Balakrishnan will also call on Pakistan’s leadership, the FO said. Pakistan and Singapore maintain cordial bilateral relations based on mutual respect and longstanding friendship. The visit underscores the shared commitment of the two countries to deepening and diversifying their bilateral partnership, it added. DPM Dar last spoke to Balakrishnan in May, requesting Singapore’s support in facilitating the “welfare and repatriation” of 11 Pakistanis and 20 Iranians aboard vessels seized by the United States.

items.title: Électricité | Tourner la page des coupures et planifier l’été 2027
items.description: L’addition a été lourde pour le tissu économique tunisien. Selon l’enquête de l’ Institut arabe des chefs d’entreprises (IACE) , dont les résultats ont été présentés lors de son Tunis Forum annuel, tenu le 26 octobre 2026, sous le thème stratégique «La Tunisie dans la géopolitique de l'énergie», les coupures d’électricité de l’été dernier ont généré une perte moyenne de 13 jours d’activité, touchant près des deux tiers des entreprises et coûtant 1 269,6 millions de dinars (MD) en valeur ajoutée directe. Face à la persistance des tensions sur le réseau pour la prochaine saison estivale, l’heure n’est plus à la fatalité, mais à une anticipation rigoureuse pour éviter que ce triste scénario ne se répète. Lotfi Sahli Les entreprises interrogées dans le cadre de cette enquête s’attendent à une récurrence des difficultés électriques en 2027. La question n’est donc plus de savoir comment récupérer les journées perdues durant l’été dernier, mais bien comment éviter que ces pertes ne se reproduisent l’été prochain. Du délestage subi au délestage planifié Afin d’éviter les coupures imprévisibles qui endommagent les machines et paralysent la production, la solution résidera dans la mise en place d’un calendrier national de délestage tournant avant le début de l’été. Ce système préventif offrira une visibilité indispensable aux industriels à travers : – des coupures régulières et annoncées : en cas de déficit de production, des interruptions programmées (par exemple, une fois par semaine par zone) permettront aux usines d’anticiper leurs livraisons, d’ajuster leurs horaires et d’effectuer sereinement leurs opérations de maintenance ; – la protection du matériel : un arrêt planifié préservera les équipements sensibles (moteurs, compresseurs, systèmes informatiques) des chocs électriques brutaux ; – la préservation des secteurs stratégiques : les entreprises exportatrices et les activités en continu bénéficieront d’un traitement spécifique afin d’éviter les ruptures d’approvisionnement et les pénalités contractuelles. Vers une flexibilité organisée du temps de travail Ce système pourrait prendre la forme d’un véritable calendrier national de gestion de la demande électrique. Les zones industrielles seraient réparties en plusieurs groupes et soumises à une rotation des interruptions lors des périodes de pointe. En contrepartie, les entreprises concernées pourraient bénéficier de règles claires en matière d’organisation du travail et de repos compensateur. Une telle démarche aurait également le mérite de replacer la question des coupures dans une logique de planification. L’expérience de 2026 a montré que le coût d’une interruption ne se limite pas à l’électricité non fournie. Il englobe les machines endommagées, la production perdue, les commandes retardées, les pénalités éventuelles, les clients qui peuvent être perdus et les investissements reportés. Pour compenser le temps de production perdu sans alourdir excessivement la charge des salariés, le dispositif s’appuiera sur une flexibilité concertée. Dans le respect du cadre légal et des conventions, certains dimanches du printemps ou de l’été pourront être intégrés, sur la base du volontariat, pour rattraper l’activité. Les heures supplémentaires ainsi réalisées ouvriront droit à un repos compensateur, répartissant l’effort sur la durée pour ne pas faire peser toute la charge sur une seule période critique. Prévenir ces pertes coûtera toujours moins cher que de réparer les dégâts (commandes annulées, investissements reportés, clients perdus…). Le véritable défi sera donc de transformer le choc de l’année passée en un modèle d'organisation pérenne. En posant dès maintenant les bases d'un calendrier clair, la Tunisie permettra à son économie de traverser la prochaine saison estivale sans subir l’imprévisibilité. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye mise sur l’héritage des Jeux et l’insertion des jeunes volontaires
items.description: À trois jours de l’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, appelle à une mobilisation nationale pour assurer le succès de cet événement historique pour le Sénégal et le continent africain. Au-delà de la compétition, le gouvernement est également appelé à préparer l’héritage des Jeux, avec un accent particulier sur l’apprentissage et l’insertion des 6 000 jeunes volontaires mobilisés. Le Sénégal entre dans la dernière ligne droite des préparatifs des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. À l’occasion du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 28 octobre, le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a invité les populations à réserver un accueil chaleureux aux délégations étrangères attendues pour cet événement sportif international. Prévue le 31 octobre au Stade du Sénégal Président Abdoulaye Wade, la cérémonie officielle d’ouverture se déroulera en présence de plusieurs chefs d’État et de gouvernement, ainsi que de la présidente et de membres du Comité international olympique (CIO). Le chef de l’État a engagé le gouvernement, les services de l’État et le Comité d’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse (COJOJ) à veiller au bon déroulement du programme sportif et culturel. Il a également réitéré son appel à l’unité nationale et à la mobilisation populaire autour de la réussite de cette manifestation, qui placera le Sénégal au centre de l’actualité sportive internationale. La délégation sénégalaise, baptisée « Team Sénégal », a reçu le drapeau national des mains du président de la République le 26 octobre, en présence de représentants du mouvement sportif. Bassirou Diomaye Faye lui a souhaité plein succès pour cette compétition. Les derniers réglages avant l'ouverture Au-delà de cet appel à la mobilisation, les autorités poursuivent le suivi des derniers préparatifs. Selon la communication du Premier ministre au Conseil des ministres, plusieurs opérations restent au centre de l’attention gouvernementale, notamment la salubrité et la propreté des sites, les dispositifs sanitaires et de secours, le transport ainsi que l’accueil et l’hébergement des délégations officielles et des invités. Les ministres ont été invités à assurer une supervision étroite des opérations relevant de leurs compétences et à mettre en place un dispositif de veille pendant toute la durée des Jeux, afin de faciliter la remontée et la résolution des éventuelles difficultés. Le 31 octobre sera également marqué par la tenue du Sommet de Dakar consacré au thème « Sport pour le Développement », auquel le président de la République attache une importance particulière. L'héritage des Jeux au-delà des infrastructures La question de l’après-JOJ figure également parmi les priorités du gouvernement. Les ministres ont été instruits de finaliser, sous la supervision de la Primature, la stratégie d’héritage des Jeux dans toutes ses dimensions, au-delà des seules infrastructures sportives. Un accent particulier sera mis sur la mise en place d’un dispositif d’apprentissage et d’insertion pour les 6 000 jeunes volontaires mobilisés dans le cadre de l’événement. Cette orientation place la valorisation des compétences acquises par ces jeunes parmi les enjeux de l’après-compétition. Les autorités ont également demandé aux différents départements ministériels de préserver la documentation produite durant les préparatifs, afin de capitaliser les connaissances et l’expérience acquises pour l’organisation de futurs événements de même envergure. À travers ces orientations, le gouvernement entend ainsi préparer non seulement le bon déroulement des JOJ Dakar 2026, mais aussi les retombées de cette première organisation olympique sur le continent africain. L’enjeu sera de faire de cet événement un levier durable pour la jeunesse, le sport et le rayonnement international du Sénégal.

items.title: Kankan : le tradi-praticien El Hadj Ibrahima Baba Sangaré retrouvé mort dans son véhicule à Sogbè
items.description: Un tradi-praticien identifié comme El Hadj Ibrahima Baba Sangaré a été retrouvé inerte dans son véhicule, ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026, au quartier Sogbè, à Kankan. Alertées par un citoyen, les autorités locales et les forces de sécurité se sont rendues sur les lieux. Transporté à l’hôpital régional de Kankan, l’homme était déjà décédé avant son arrivée, selon une source médicale. Les circonstances exactes de ce décès restent à éclaircir. Toutefois, un témoin affirme avoir aperçu le conducteur peu avant sa découverte et décrit un comportement inhabituel au volant. Moussa Condé, témoin : « Il a failli me renverser » Moussa Condé raconte avoir croisé le véhicule alors qu’il se rendait chez un ami. Selon son témoignage, le conducteur aurait manqué de le heurter avant de poursuivre sa route. « Quand je partais chez un ami, il a failli me renverser sur la chaussée. Je me suis demandé s’il savait conduire. Quelques instants après, je l’ai dépassé. Il a également failli heurter des élèves et aurait touché l’un d’entre eux. Son rétroviseur s’est cassé », témoigne-t-il. Poursuivant son récit, Moussa Condé explique que le conducteur se serait arrêté un peu plus loin, avant de descendre de son véhicule pour récupérer un objet tombé. « Il a ouvert le véhicule, il est sorti pour aller chercher quelque chose qui était tombé, puis il est remonté dans sa voiture. Moi, j’ai fait deux passages et sa voiture était toujours garée au même endroit, jusqu’à cette découverte », ajoute-t-il. Ce témoignage permet de retracer certains des derniers moments au cours desquels le tradi-praticien aurait été aperçu, sans toutefois établir de lien entre les faits rapportés et son décès. Moussa Sacko, adjoint au chef de quartier : « La personne ne réagissait pas » Selon Moussa Sacko, adjoint au chef de quartier, l’alerte a été donnée par un citoyen qui l’a informé de la présence d’un homme immobile dans un véhicule. « Ce soir, vers 17 heures, j’ai reçu l’appel d’un citoyen m’informant qu’il y avait une situation particulière. Je suis venu et j’ai trouvé une personne dans le véhicule, couchée sur le côté. Comme l’endroit se trouvait à proximité de la Direction de la police judiciaire (DPJ), j’ai informé les agents. Ils sont venus et nous avons contacté le commissariat central. Nous avons ouvert la portière, mais la personne ne réagissait pas », explique-t-il. L’adjoint au chef de quartier précise toutefois qu’au moment de la découverte, il n’était pas en mesure de confirmer si l’homme était vivant ou décédé. « La question de savoir s’il était vivant ou non, ce sont les médecins qui peuvent la confirmer », souligne-t-il. Sékou Mariam Sagno commissaire central : le procureur informé Informée de la situation, la police a saisi le procureur de la République avant de dépêcher les services compétents sur les lieux. Le commissaire central de police de Kankan, Sékou Mariam Asayou, est revenu sur les circonstances de l’intervention. Selon lui, la police a été informée par le chef du commissariat urbain de Missira, lui-même alerté par le chef de quartier , dans le secteur de Sogbè. « Nous avons été informés par le chef du commissariat urbain de Missira. À son tour, il avait été informé par le chef de quartier qu’un monsieur se trouvait dans un véhicule et semblait être couché. C’est ainsi que la police a informé le procureur de la République et que nous nous sommes rendus sur les lieux », a-t-il expliqué. Sur place, les forces de sécurité ont constaté la présence d’un homme identifié comme El Hadj Ibrahima Baba Sangaré, à bord d’une voiture de marque Toyota. Les sapeurs-pompiers et le personnel médical ont également été mobilisés pour les constatations. Le commissaire central indique que, sur la base des premières informations recueillies, l’homme serait descendu de son véhicule avant d’y remonter. La voiture étant restée immobilisée pendant un certain temps, des personnes se seraient approchées pour vérifier la situation avant d’alerter les autorités. « Après toutes les constatations, il a été décidé, avec l’avis du procureur de la République, de transporter le monsieur à l’hôpital pour faire des examens », précise-t-il. Interrogé sur l’état de santé du tradi-praticien au moment de son évacuation, le commissaire central a rappelé que seule l’équipe médicale pouvait apporter une confirmation. Une source médicale confirme le décès Jointe au téléphone, une source médicale de l’hôpital régional de Kankan a confirmé qu’El Hadj Ibrahima Baba Sangaré était déjà décédé avant son arrivée dans l’établissement. « Il était déjà décédé avant qu’il n’arrive à l’hôpital régional de Kankan. C’était un dépôt de corps », a indiqué cette source. Pour l’heure, les causes du décès n’ont pas été officiellement établies. Les circonstances de cet incident restent donc à éclaircir. items.title: Football fan jailed for threats over Di Maria return to Argentina
items.description: An Argentine court jailed a football supporter for seven and a half years on Wednesday for threatening Angel Di Maria in 2024 in a bid to stop the World Cup winner returning to Argentina at the end of his career. A court in Rosario found Sergio Di Vanni, 45, guilty of ordering acts of intimidation against Di Maria’s family with the aim of dissuading the former Argentina international from returning from abroad to play for a rival club. Di Maria was playing for Benfica at the time, in March 2024, but was considering a return to his boyhood club Rosario Central, a move he eventually completed in 2025. Rosario Central and Newell’s Old Boys, Lionel Messi’s childhood club, are the two major teams in Rosario and fierce local rivals. The threats included gunshots fired near a gated community where Di Maria owns a property and the dumping of a pig’s head bearing a bullet wound outside an estate agency run by his sister, alongside a message threatening his daughter. A 25-year-old woman, Belen Gutierrez, identified by prosecutors as one of the perpetrators, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in June after entering a plea agreement. A third suspect remains in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors alleged the two carried out the threats in exchange for four million pesos ($2,600). According to the prosecution, the intimidation campaign was linked to an internal power struggle among Newell’s ultras. Di Vanni’s sentence also covered separate offences related to his involvement in the supporters’ group. Following the threats, Di Maria initially abandoned plans to return to Argentina for the safety of his family. He ultimately reversed that decision and, now 38, has spent the past two seasons at Rosario Central, helping the club win the Argentine title at the end of 2025. items.title: ADC accuses Mbah of anti-people policies in Enugu
items.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Enugu State Government of implementing anti-people policies, alleging that the administration of Governor Peter Mbah has worsened the hardship faced by residents. The party’s 2027 governorship candidate, Chief Ocho Obodoeze, made the allegations in a statement issued by his media team and signed by Paul Anigbogu, in which he described the state government’s policies as “anti-people” and “draconian”. Obodoeze alleged that the policies had inflicted physical and psychological hardship on residents rather than improving their living conditions, contrary to the promises made by the governor during the 2023 election campaign. He recalled that Mbah had promised to end perennial water scarcity and provide clean, running pipe-borne water to every household and neighbourhood in Enugu metropolis within 180 days of assuming office, with plans to extend the project to other parts of the state, including Nsukka, Udi and Awgu. The ADC candidate, however, accused the administration of failing to fulfil the promise. He also criticised the demolition of properties and trading locations across the state, alleging that affected residents and business owners were left without adequate compensation or alternative means of livelihood. According to him, demolitions at Old Park and Gariki in Enugu, as well as Ogige Market in Nsukka, displaced residents and traders, leaving thousands without their sources of income. He claimed that some of those affected suffered depression, while others reportedly died, which he attributed to the loss of their livelihoods and the absence of relief or compensation. Obodoeze further accused the state government of imposing multiple taxes on traders, survivors of the demolitions, commercial tricycle operators and bus operators, describing the situation as excessive. He also questioned the state government’s appointment and contract-award practices, alleging that non-indigenes had been favoured over qualified people from Enugu State. “While Enugu people were the ones bearing the brunt of the ruthless and inhuman taxation of the government, our governor favoured non-Enugu indigenes in appointments and contracts,” he said. The ADC candidate questioned whether qualified personnel could not be found among the state’s population of more than 4.6 million people to occupy key government positions. He also alleged that major government contracts, including the construction of smart schools, had been awarded to contractors from outside the state, some of whom he accused of delivering substandard work. Obodoeze promised to investigate the contracts and seek the recovery of outstanding funds if elected governor in 2027. The ADC candidate also expressed concern about the welfare of teachers in the state, claiming that Enugu teachers were among the poorest-paid in Nigeria. On the political front, he urged the state government to stop what he described as the suppression of opposition parties and ensure a level playing field ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also alleged that political violence had increased in the state since the current political season began, claiming that opposition parties were among the primary targets. Obodoeze said an ADC-led government would prioritise security, improve the welfare of teachers, other public workers and pensioners, and invest in infrastructure across sectors. He added that his administration would invest heavily in agriculture and industrialisation to strengthen food security, expand exports, stimulate economic activities and create jobs. The governorship hopeful further pledged that 98 per cent of appointments and contracts under his administration would be reserved for Enugu indigenes, saying the policy would empower local residents and give them opportunities similar to those available to indigenes in other states. The allegations were contained in the ADC candidate’s statement. The statement did not include a response from the Enugu State Government to the claims. items.title: Relance économique :le Président Diomaye Faye insiste sur l’apurement de la dette intérieure et la reprise des chantiers
items.description: Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, demande au gouvernement d’accélérer la relance des activités économiques, de reprendre les chantiers à l’arrêt et de procéder à l’apurement rapide de la dette intérieure. Lors du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 28 octobre, il a également insisté sur le financement des campagnes agricoles et horticoles ainsi que sur l’exécution des investissements publics prioritaires. La relance économique figure parmi les priorités fixées par le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, au gouvernement. Lors du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 28 octobre, le chef de l’État a demandé au Premier ministre de prendre les mesures nécessaires pour accélérer les activités économiques et la mise en œuvre des projets publics, notamment ceux inscrits dans les orientations budgétaires de 2026 et de 2027. Parmi les instructions présidentielles figure l’apurement rapide de la dette intérieure, en concertation avec les organisations représentatives du secteur privé. Cette mesure vise à placer le règlement des engagements de l’État envers les entreprises au cœur des efforts de relance économique. Le président de la République a également insisté sur la nécessité de mener des actions concertées pour relancer les activités économiques et les chantiers à l’arrêt. Une orientation qui concerne notamment la poursuite des investissements publics et l’accélération des projets dans les secteurs prioritaires. Dans cette perspective, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a demandé une évaluation intégrale de la mise en œuvre du Plan de redressement économique et social (PRES), ainsi qu’un état des lieux du déploiement des projets relevant de l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050. Le chef de l’État entend ainsi disposer d’un bilan de l’avancement de ces programmes et accélérer leur exécution. Les investissements publics et les campagnes agricoles en ligne de mire Les infrastructures sociales figurent également parmi les priorités présidentielles. Le chef de l’État a demandé au gouvernement d’intensifier la réalisation et l’équipement des établissements publics de santé, des universités, des Instituts supérieurs d’enseignement professionnel (ISEP) et des écoles modernes, avec des personnels qualifiés. Il a aussi insisté sur l’accélération des projets d’électrification rurale et d’hydraulique, en particulier le Grand Transfert d’eau vers l’agglomération de Touba-Mbacké et le nouveau programme de forages multivillages. Le financement des campagnes de commercialisation des produits agricoles et horticoles figure parmi les autres dossiers soumis à l’attention du gouvernement. Cette orientation place les besoins des filières agricoles parmi les leviers identifiés pour soutenir l’activité économique. En parallèle, le président de la République a demandé au Premier ministre de faire le bilan d’étape du New Deal technologique et d’accélérer la rationalisation des secteurs public et parapublic. La stabilité sociale comme condition de la relance Bassirou Diomaye Faye a, par ailleurs, insisté sur la nécessité de préserver un climat social serein pour accompagner la reprise des activités économiques. Il a invité le gouvernement à poursuivre le dialogue avec les centrales syndicales afin de parvenir à des consensus durables. Le Premier ministre devra assurer un suivi rapproché de ce dialogue dans le cadre du Pacte de stabilité sociale pour une croissance inclusive et durable, signé le 1er mai 2025. À travers ces instructions, le chef de l’État place la reprise de l’activité économique, le règlement de la dette intérieure et l’accélération des investissements publics au centre des priorités gouvernementales. La mise en œuvre de ces orientations devra notamment se traduire par la relance des chantiers, l’avancement des projets prioritaires et le soutien aux acteurs économiques.

items.title: US: New Hurdles to Having Votes Counted
items.description: Click to expand Image US election workers open and inspect mail-in ballot envelopes during processing inside the Maricopa County Tabulation and Election Center (MCTEC) on Election Day, November 5, 2024, in Phoenix, Arizona. © 2024 Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images (Washington, DC) – US states’ use of a tool to verify citizenship that is marred by inaccurate and incomplete data is creating new hurdles for the right to vote with the midterm elections only days away, Human Rights Watch said today. The Supreme Court ruled in late September 2026 that states could use the tool, Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE), to screen lists of registered voters for citizenship status, at least for the time being. “The use of the SAVE tool is causing new hurdles for some voters,” said Katherine La Puente, US democracy researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Sending vaguely worded letters as early voting began or offering federal-only ballots to some registered voters risks a discriminatory impact on people’s right to vote.” The Trump administration expanded use of the problematic SAVE online system, which previously had been used only for public benefits and was not designed for verifying voter eligibility, in 2025 to now use it for these purposes. Some states have adopted their use of SAVE to verify voter eligibility, and the recent Supreme Court ruling has allowed its use for individualized inquiries. Federal law does not require proof of citizenship when registering to vote, but states have passed these laws requiring proof for state and local races, resulting in bifurcated voter systems. In Utah, thousands of voters flagged by the SAVE database were sent notification letters over the summer, and in October over 4,000 who didn’t respond were mailed ballots with only federal races. In South Dakota, nearly 6,000 voters have been categorized as federal-only voters as well as 47,000 in Arizona. In Utah and Arizona, they can provide proof of citizenship and vote in person on Election Day but can’t vote by mail, a method relied on by most voters. In North Carolina, vaguely worded letters sent to 1,400 registered voters flagged through SAVE asking for proof of citizenship may deter people from going to the polls. Earlier in 2026, Utah audited its voter rolls, finding that it could not verify the citizenship status of over 5,000 registered voters. It sent them letters indicating that they needed to provide documentary proof of citizenship. Many were older voters who did not need documentation when they registered to vote. Fewer than 2,000 have responded. The others will receive ballots only for federal offices. In South Dakota, new state laws requiring documentary proof of citizenship and residential addresses quadrupled the voters in the “federal-only” category because they did not submit proof of citizenship or list a mail forwarding service or P.O. Box as their address when they registered. County clerks sent notification letters to these voters that misstated the reasons for their change in status. After advocates filed a federal lawsuit against the state, officials issued corrected notices in September. South Dakota’s online Voter Information Portal does not tell voters if they are registered as federal-only and changes were only allowed until the state’s October 19 registration deadline. The North Carolina State Board of Elections sent letters to nearly 1,400 registered voters flagged through SAVE just two days before early voting began on October 15. The board of elections has since confirmed that all citizens are still entitled to vote even as it resolves these queries, and voting rights groups are emphasizing that all those flagged should still be able to vote. But people who got the letters may think they cannot vote or may run into issues at the polls. In July, with less than a month to the August primary, the director of Alaska’s Division of Elections admitted in a legislative hearing that her office had mailed letters to more than 3,000 voters asking to confirm their citizenship and marked them inactive. Though hundreds have had their registration restored, others will only be able to vote with a questioned ballot, which is only counted once the voter’s eligibility is verified. Earlier in 2026, a new law took effect in Ohio that requires the Office of the Secretary of State to review its voter registration database at least monthly and direct elections officials to promptly cancel a flagged person’s registration. Citizen groups have raised concerns that this could lead to mistaken removals close to elections, with 75 people removed in September and 90 in October. In Arizona, the Maricopa County recorder flagged 207 voters identified through SAVE as “not eligible” to vote, which means the voters would stay on the rolls, but would not receive mail-in ballots and would need to use a provisional ballot. Of an initial investigation of 60 of these voters, the Maricopa County attorney determined at least 52 were citizens. But the county did not restore some people’s eligibility until the state attorney general filed suit and a resolution was negotiated. Arizona has required proof of citizenship to register to vote in state and local elections since 2004. Clean Elections Arizona estimates that 47,000 voters are now in this federal-only category. Naturalized citizens, people who automatically became citizens during childhood when their parents naturalized, US citizens born abroad, and those without easy access to documentation are particularly at risk as a result of these moves. Often, individuals who secured their citizenship through a parent’s naturalization or at birth abroad may not have access to the original documents confirming their status, which they obtained as children. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which the United States has ratified, requires governments to ensure the right to vote without unreasonable restrictions or discrimination. The International Convention on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination requires the United States to eliminate racial discrimination and to guarantee the right to vote “without distinction as to race, colour, or national or ethnic origin.” In its concluding observations for its review of the United States in 2022, the Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination expressed concern about practices that “constrain the exercise of the right to vote with a disproportionate impact on people of African descent, indigenous peoples, persons of Hispanic/Latino origin and other ethnic minorities,” and said that the United States should “facilitate access to voting and eliminate unreasonable restrictions to the exercise of the right to vote.” A survey by the Brennan Center found that more than 9 percent of those polled did not have proof of citizenship readily available, which would mean 21.3 million people nationally if the results are accurate. A study by the Center for American Progress found that fewer than half of US citizens held a valid US passport in 2024. Communities of color, immigrants, low-income, and older people are less likely to have identity documents such as passports or birth certificates. There is no evidence of widespread, unlawful voting by noncitizens in US elections, and such claims have been disproven in other states like Nevada and Missouri. Nationwide, CBS News reported, 156 people had been charged with offenses related to voter fraud since January 2025, out of approximately 227 million registered voters. Other statements and actions made by the Trump administration leading up to the elections could deter people from voting. In several states, Department of Homeland Security (DHS) agents have questioned people in their homes about their immigration status and voting history, though a judge recently restricted these operations in nine states. Neither President Donald Trump nor the heads of the DHS and the Federal Bureau of Investigation have been willing to rule out the possibility that federal agents, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers, may be at polling places. “Election officials should take steps to eliminate hurdles to vote and ensure that voters feel confident to go to the polls,” La Puente said.

items.title: US judge rejects Trump admin interference in California midterm vote
items.description: A federal judge on Wednesday rejected the US Department of Justice’s efforts to set aside the ballots of more than 20,000 California voters it said might not be citizens, slamming the move as brazen pre-election “interference.” The case sparked an uproar ahead of the November 3 midterms, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is at risk of losing its control of Congress, and appears to represent another attempt to cast doubt on electoral results. Democratic Party leaders have sued the Trump administration over the request, accusing Republicans of aiming “threats and intimidation” at state and local officials before the vote. US District Judge David O. Carter agreed, refusing to order the seizure of the ballots and siding with the government of Democratic-led California. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch,” Carter wrote in his decision. “Constitutional rights and our democracy are at stake. The public interest favors their protection,” he added. Those registered on California’s voter roles “must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors.” The federal government in recent months had accused California of having 190,000 illegal voters on its books. It recently revised the figure to 20,000 and filed an emergency lawsuit about 10 days ago — after early voting had begun — to stop the state from sending ballots to them. A similar controversy arose in neighboring Nevada, where the allegations fizzled. The Trump administration had initially identified 16,000 non-citizen voters there, but after verification procedures that number dropped to 185 — and then to zero. “The DOJ’s actions are indicative of a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference by federal officials,” Carter wrote in his decision. For months, Trump — who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Joe Biden in 2020 — has been claiming that there will be fraud in this year’s midterms. Studies repeatedly show that while rare cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are miniscule and do not influence election results. AFP The post US judge rejects Trump admin interference in California midterm vote appeared first on Vanguard News .
