items.title: Arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi, others out in Radio Pakistan attack case
items.description: PESHAWAR: An anti-terrorism court on Wednesday issued arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi, the ex-chief minister who was rendered nonfunctional after the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and four other PTI leaders in the Radio Pakistan attack case . The prosecution had earlier placed the supplementary charge-sheet on the court record, but the hearing was adjourned until Oct 28 due to the judge’s absence. Besides Mr Afridi, the supplementary challan names former provincial ministers Taimoor Saleem Jhagra and Kamran Bangash, PTI Peshawar district president Irfan Saleem and party activist Amir Khan Chamkani. None of them was initially named in the FIR or the charge-sheet. When the matter came up for hearing on Wednesday, Judge Wali Mohammad Khan directed the issuance of warrants as the five newly nominated accused have yet to be arrested. The court order stated that the police had submitted a supplementary charge-sheet against the five accused, who had not been arrested, and directed that warrants be issued under Section 204 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Senior lawyer Shabbir Hussain Gigyani appeared for the Pakis­tan Broadcasting Corporation, while senior public prosecutor Manzoor Alam Khan represented the state. Advocate Ali Zaman appeared for the accused. The charge-sheet follows findings by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency and Nadra concerning video clips purportedly showing the incident and profile pictures of the suspects. According to investigation officer DSP Khushal Khan’s report, Radio Pakistan Peshawar station director Tufail Ahmad recorded a supplementary statement in light of the forensic findings, nominating the five men as accused. The forensic examination was ordered on Dec 12, 2025, on an application filed by Mr Gigyani. The PFSA subsequently concluded that the facial features of the five men matched those of suspects seen allegedly participating in the rioting in the video footage. Nadra’s report identified CNIC numbers apparently belonging to the men and described them as probable matches for the profile pictures submitted for examination. While Mr Gigyani maintained that the footage related to the attack on the Radio Pakistan building, PTI leaders questioned its authenticity, arguing that the clips did not pertain to the May 10, 2023, incident, which occurred after the arrest of former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan. After the directive for the issuance of arrest warrants, the court fixed Nov 4 for the next hearing. Meanwhile, a petition challenging Mr Afridi’s alleged illegal detention or enforced disappearance remains pending before the Peshawar High Court. Published in Dawn, October 29th, 2026

items.title: Coupe inter ministérielle et institutions : Le MATM s’adjuge le titre en maracana
items.description: La 12 e édition de la coupe inter ministérielle et institutions organisée par le ministère des sports, de la jeunesse et de l’emploi, a connu son apothéose le mardi 27 octobre 2026 à l’Institut supérieur des sports et de développement humain, de Ouagadougou. La compétition a concerné le maracana, le volley-ball et la pétanque. En maracana, le Ministère de l’Administration Territoriale et de la Mobilité (MATM) a dominé le ministère de la santé par trois (03) buts à zéro (0). La finale a connu la présence du ministre en charge des sports et celui de la santé. Ce sont 31 ministères et institutions qui se sont affrontées durant plus d’un mois dans trois (03) disciplines sportives, à savoir la pétanque, le volley-ball et le maracana. En finale maracana, le MATM n’a pas eu de difficultés devant celui de la santé. Dès la première période, il assure avec deux (02) buts. En seconde période, il ajoute un (01) but sans en n’encaisser. Le MATM est vainqueur de cette 12 e édition, la santé est vice champion. La 3 e place revient au ministère des sports, de la jeunesse et de l’emploi et le ministère de la sécurité est classé 4 e . En volley-ball, la première place échoit au ministère de la sécurité. Le ministère des sports, de la jeunesse et de l’emploi est 2 e . Le ministère de la guerre et de la défense patriotique arrive à la 3 e place. La présidence du Faso est 4 e . Côté récompense, chaque équipe de ces deux (02) disciplines classée première reçoit 300 000 FCFA, le trophée ainsi que des médailles d’or. Chaque 2 e repart avec 200 000 FCFA ainsi que des médailles d’argent. Les 3 e au classement empochent chacun 150 000 FCFA et des médailles de bronze. Pour la 4 e place, c’est 100 000 FCFA qui leur revient. En pétanque, c’est l’ASCELC qui est plus droite et elle arrive première. Pour cette place, elle jubile avec 150 000 FCFA, des médailles d’or et le trophée. Le ministère de la sécurité est sa dauphine et se console avec 100 000 FCFA ainsi que des médailles d’argent. Le MENAPLN est 3 e avec 75 000 FCFA en sus des médailles de bronze. Le ministère de la guerre et de la défense patriotique est 4 e . Elle repart avec dans sa gibecière 50 000 FCFA. La ministre des sports, de la jeunesse et de l’emploi, Annick Pikbougoum soutient que ce rendez-vous sportif, réunit les travailleurs des ministères et institutions autour des valeurs de discipline, de solidarité et de dépassement de soi. Et qu’il constitue une belle illustration de la place que l’on entend accorder au sport dans les administrations. L’intérêt particulier que vous portez au sport pour tous, et à l'épanouissement des travailleurs, de la volonté d'étendre la pratique du sport à l'ensemble des réseaux sociaux professionnels s'inscrit en droite ligne de la vision du gouvernement et de la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale du sport >> explique Annick Pikbougoum. Dans son intervention, la première responsable du département du sport, explique qu’il s'agit notamment de promouvoir et de créer des conditions propices au développement des activités physiques et récréatives au sein des administrations publiques. Ce qui permet de contribuer au maintien des travailleurs en bonne santé et de renforcer leurs engagements au service de la nation. Toutes les équipes participantes ont reçu du matériel, afin de leur permettre de pratiquer pleinement le sport pour tous dans les différents ministères et institutions. items.title: IATA : près d’un passager sur deux utilise l’IA dans la préparation des voyages
items.description: L’intelligence artificielle (IA) s’impose progressivement comme un outil courant dans la préparation des voyages, près d’un passager sur deux dans le monde (49%) déclarant y avoir eu recours, selon les résultats de l’Enquête mondiale 2026 auprès des passagers, publiés mercredi par l’Association internationale du transport aérien (IATA). Réalisée auprès de plus de 10.000 personnes dans plus de 200 pays, cette enquête révèle que 21% des voyageurs utilisent l’IA pour rechercher des vols vers une destination précise, 19% pour trouver les tarifs les plus avantageux et 17% pour découvrir de nouvelles destinations. “Les passagers adoptent les technologies pour faciliter leurs voyages. L’IA devient un outil courant de planification, tandis que la biométrie et l’identité numérique contribuent à fluidifier les parcours dans les aéroports”, a souligné Nick Careen, vice-président principal chargé des opérations, de la sûreté et de la sécurité à l’IATA. L’Organisation, basée à Genève, souligne ainsi l’évolution des habitudes des voyageurs, qui privilégient des solutions numériques permettant de simplifier les démarches et de personnaliser les services, tout en appelant les compagnies aériennes à mieux intégrer leurs offres dans les outils d’IA et à faciliter la conversion des recherches en réservations. L’enquête met également en évidence la progression de la biométrie, utilisée au moins une fois au cours des douze derniers mois par 58% des passagers interrogés, contre 50% en 2025 et 34% en 2022. Parmi les voyageurs ayant expérimenté cette technologie, 87% se déclarent satisfaits, tandis que 78% se disent disposés à partager leurs données biométriques si cela leur permet d’éviter de présenter plusieurs fois leur passeport ou leur carte d’embarquement. L’intérêt pour les passeports numériques est également marqué, 84% des répondants souhaitant les utiliser pour l’enregistrement en ligne. Toutefois, la protection des données demeure une préoccupation majeure : 59% des personnes interrogées craignent les violations de données, 49% redoutent le partage de leurs informations avec d’autres organisations et 41% estiment manquer de clarté sur leur traitement. Par ailleurs, les formalités d’entrée constituent un obstacle croissant à la mobilité internationale : 43% des voyageurs déclarent avoir renoncé à visiter une destination en raison des exigences migratoires, contre 33% en 2025. Parmi eux, 53% jugent les procédures trop complexes. Face à ces difficultés, 86% des répondants se disent prêts à transmettre leurs informations migratoires par voie numérique avant leur départ, tandis que 60% privilégient une demande de visa en ligne. L’IATA appelle ainsi les gouvernements à simplifier les formalités d’entrée, à réduire les contrôles redondants et à accélérer l’adoption de documents de voyage numériques sécurisés reposant sur des normes communes, afin de concilier fluidité des déplacements, efficacité des procédures et protection des données personnelles. The post IATA : près d’un passager sur deux utilise l’IA dans la préparation des voyages appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Health ministry scraps ‘flawed’ vaccine tender
items.description: • Border Health Services vaccination setup abolished; new ministry tender due in a month • Officials arrested for bypassing ministry via parallel procurement committees • Pilgrims asked to arrange jabs thru travel agents ISLAMABAD: The Ministry of National Health Services has decided to issue a new procurement tender for meningococcal meningitis and influenza vaccines for overseas travellers within a month, following its decision to abolish the existing vaccination setup through Border Health Services (BHS). The decision follows a high-level inquiry ordered by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif into the BHS. The probe exposed severe flaws and financial irregularities in a previously awarded public-private partnership contract. Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal confirmed that authorities have halted the current vaccination process for religious pilgrims and overseas job seekers. Furthermore, all BHS officials involved in floating the unauthorised tender have been arrested for bypassing ministry oversight. “I can assure that they will be fixed for keeping the ministry in the dark,” Mr Kamal said. “I am carrying a good reputation and have remained clean throughout my career. So I will not tolerate any attempt to defame me.” With the BHS system dismantled, the ministry has directed pilgrims to arrange their mandatory vaccinations directly through their travel agents until the ministry’s central procurement committee floats a replacement tender. The inquiry by the prime minister was triggered by allegations that the new contract inflated vaccination costs to approximately Rs4,500 per pilgrim, up sharply from around Rs1,250 per dose under the previous arrangement. Meanwhile, seven companies petitioned the Islamabad High Court challenging alleged irregularities in the bidding process. A five-member inquiry committee chaired by the Cabinet Division secretary examined the legal basis, rationale and approvals for the contract. The panel included the Intelli­gence Bureau director general, the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) chief executive officer, the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority managing director and a representative from the Attorney General’s Office. Official documents collected by the inquiry committee and reviewed by Dawn reveal that BHS officials created parallel committees to bypass federal oversight. On May 9, the health ministry established an official six-member procurement committee chaired by BHS Director Dr Mir Muhammad Hassan Builo, alongside a grievance committee led by the federal director general of health. However, on June 10, BHS unilaterally formed its own procurement committee chaired by Dr Pardeep Kumar and a separate redressal committee led by Dr Shahbaz Ahmed Hashmi, proceeding to float the tender independently. A senior ministry official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, claimed the health ministry was kept in the dark. “The major violation was that the PPRA rules were followed for a public-private partnership. In fact, Public Private Partnership Authority rules should have been applied for the tender,” the official explained. “As per the agreement, the private company had to procure the vaccine, and the amount had to be deposited in a National Database and Registration Authority accou­­nt. Nadra would then cut its charges and distribute the share between BHS and the private company. The positive thing was that not a single rupee had to be spent from the exchequer.” The official noted the 1,250-rupee price in 2026 occurred because a company secured cheaper stock. Previously, per-dose charges for meningitis vaccines were Rs2,555 in 2025, Rs2,244 in 2024, Rs2,476 in 2023, and Rs2,550 in 2022. Influ­enza vaccines cost Rs1,426 in 2025 and Rs1,670 in 2024. Another official noted the tender will be re-advertised but argued the seven petitioning companies should provide the 1,250-rupee rate they cited. He noted the vaccine’s maximum retail price is around Rs1,300, but it was historically sold for over Rs2,000. Uncoordinated past procurements triggered the use of fake vaccination certificates, causing trouble for pilgrims and embarrassment for the federal government. Published in Dawn, October 29th, 2026

items.title: RDC / Vague de défections dans l’armée : Après le Général Kamazi, le Colonel Dem Umba Ndolo Ghislain bascule dans le FRN de Joseph Kabila
items.description: Une dynamique d'effritement touche le commandement des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) dans la province du Tanganyika. Après le ralliement du Général Kamazi, un autre officier supérieur, le Colonel Dem Umba Ndolo Ghislain — commandant adjoint en charge des opérations et du renseignement de la 61ᵉ brigade d'infanterie basée à Nyunzu , a officiellement fait défection pour rejoindre le Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), un mouvement associé à l'ancien président Joseph Kabila. Actuellement localisé à Goma, ce haut gradé vient allonger la liste croissante des militaires prenant leurs distances avec l'armée régulière. Le nombre de militaires faisant défection au sein des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ne cesse de s'accroître. La 61ᵉ brigade d'infanterie des Forces terrestres, positionnée à Nyunzu dans la province du Tanganyika, subit le départ direct de ses responsables opérationnels. En effet, les deux officiers supérieurs concernés, le Général Kamazi et le Colonel Dem Umba Ndolo Ghislain, occupaient précisément les fonctions stratégiques de gestion des opérations militaires et du renseignement au sein de cette unité. Dernier fait marquant en date, le Colonel Dem Umba Ndolo Ghislain a formellement rompu ses engagements envers les forces d'État. Avant sa désertion, cet officier exerçait la charge de commandant second et adjoint des opérations et du renseignement de la 61ᵉ brigade. Selon les informations disponibles, le colonel a fait allégeance au mouvement rebelle et se trouverait désormais dans la ville de Goma, scellant ainsi son départ effectif des rangs des FARDC. Ce double mouvement de défection vient consolider les effectifs du Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN / M23). Ce rassemblement armé, dirigé et associé à l'ancien président de la RDC, Joseph Kabila, enregistre ainsi l'adhésion successive du Général Kamazi puis du Colonel Dem Umba Ndolo Ghislain. L'arrivée de ces experts du renseignement et de la conduite des opérations au sein de la rébellion illustre un glissement inquiétant de cadres militaires vers les forces opposées à l'armée régulière. items.title: Russia warns Japan over 'historical distortions' in films
items.description: Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said on Wednesday that Moscow had noted repeated distortions of history in Japanese films and would take appropriate action if Tokyo continued such activities. Speaking at a regular press briefing, Zakharova cited Japanese films dealing with the Southern Kuril Islands, known as the Northern Territories in Japan, the Russo-Japanese War and Soviet intelligence operatives. She pointed to the 2003 Japanese film Spy Sorge , saying it glorified counterintelligence operations during Japan's militarist era. Russia advocates an objective interpretation of history, including in the film industry, Zakharova said, citing Red Silk , a Russian-Chinese co-production. She added that a sequel, Black Silk , was in development. Zakharova also expressed concern over Japan's remilitarization, citing increasingly frequent military exercises near Russia's borders, the deployment of short- and medium-range missile systems during drills, and Japan's refusal to recognize the outcome of World War II. Moscow is closely monitoring these developments, which it considers detrimental to its security interests, she said. (Cover: File photo of Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova. /VCG)

items.title: Vance contacts Iranian security chief to restart peace talks
items.description: US Vice President JD Vance has contacted Iranian security chief to revive peace talks that could stave off a renewed American assault on Iran, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported on Wednesday. Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, the WSJ reported, in a move that one of the newspaper's sources said was directed by President Donald Trump. The letter – as well as subsequent talks between US and Iranian officials – focused on a possible framework for negotiations rather than specifics of a peace proposal, the report said. The WSJ also reported Wednesday that Washington had told several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a possible "short, intense military campaign" against Iran after the US midterm elections on November 3. But the newspaper, citing people briefed on the conversations, said Trump had not made a final decision. Meanwhile, Iran's military has warned it would retaliate more widely against any new attack, with Rezaei saying it could strike US-related infrastructure including data centers and other artificial intelligence targets. The United States and Israel launched the war against Iran in late February, which has severely disrupted energy shipments from Gulf countries, causing global economic fallout. Iran began blockading the key Strait of Hormuz waterway, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel, after the conflict began and regularly attacks vessels that attempt to cross without its authorization. The United States has maintained a naval blockade of Iranian ports, seeking to squeeze the country's economy. (With input from AFP)

Sénégal : Le PASTEF dénonce des menaces d’élimination visant Ousmane Sonko
items.description: Dans un communiqué officiel n° 015 – 2026/BPN/PASTEF rendu public le 28 octobre 2026, le bureau politique national de PASTEF – Les Patriotes dénonce avec véhémence des déclarations attribuées à Arona Coumba Ndoffène Diouf, membre de la formation présidentielle Kiiraay. Ce dernier est accusé d'avoir publiquement demandé aux responsables de son parti d'orchestrer un complot visant à éliminer Ousmane Sonko, président de l'Assemblée nationale et deuxième personnalité de l'État. Qualifiant ces propos d'atteinte caractérisée à la sûreté de l'État, PASTEF invite le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, à faire cesser ces dérives et saisit le Procureur de la République près le Tribunal de Dakar pour une application stricte de la loi. La scène politique sénégalaise est traversée par une vive secousse à la suite de la diffusion du communiqué officiel n° 015 – 2026/BPN/PASTEF signé par le bureau politique de PASTEF – Les Patriotes à Dakar. Au cœur de cette vive alerte, la direction du parti dénonce fermement des propos jugés extrêmement dangereux tenus par Arona Coumba Ndoffène Diouf, cadre membre du parti présidentiel Kiiraay. Selon PASTEF, l'intéressé aurait publiquement appelé les dirigeants de sa formation politique à mettre en œuvre une cabale visant l'élimination physique du leader de PASTEF et président de l'Assemblée nationale, Ousmane Sonko. Pour les responsables de PASTEF, cette prise de parole n'est pas un acte isolé mais s'inscrit dans un climat d'escalade verbale. Le parti s'insurge contre la banalisation des discours de haine colportés par des membres de la mouvance présidentielle, accusés d'inciter le chef de l'État à utiliser la force publique pour paralyser les activités politiques de PASTEF et de son président. Rappelant que les complots et tensions politiques survenus entre 2021 et 2024 ont autrefois plongé le pays dans le chaos, l'instance dirigeante de PASTEF avertit que l'impunité accordée aux auteurs des événements criminels passés réaffirme la confiance de ceux qui prônent aujourd'hui la violence pour tenter de freiner un soutien populaire massif. Qualifiant ces menaces d'incrimination d'atteinte directe à la sûreté de l'État, le bureau politique de PASTEF exige une riposte judiciaire immédiate. Le parti demande expressément au président de la République du Sénégal, Monsieur Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, d'intervenir pour mettre un terme sans délai aux infractions à la loi émanant de membres de son parti Kiiraay. Réaffirmant sa résolution inébranlable à protéger son leader, la formation politique interpelle directement le Procureur de la République près le Parquet de Dakar afin que la rigueur de la loi soit appliquée contre les instigateurs de ces appels à la violence. L’article Sénégal : Le PASTEF dénonce des menaces d'élimination visant Ousmane Sonko est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

According to a press release issued by Nust, the distinction places Nust researchers among an international community of leading scholars whose work is contributing immensely to the advancement of knowledge and scientific progress across diverse disciplines. Notably, 16 Nust researchers have consistently featured in the rankings over successive years, demonstrating sustained scholarly impact and a long-term commitment to advancing knowledge across disciplines. “Extending his heartiest felicitations to the distinguished researchers, Rector Nust Dr Muhammad Zahid Latif remarked that the meritorious accomplishment of our truly erudite faculty and researchers has brought immense pride to Nust and the nation, and exemplifies the calibre of scholarship that continues to elevate Pakistan’s standing in the international research community,” read the press release. items.title: SC okays fresh probe into FIA role in boat tragedy
items.description: • Court upholds FST order reinstating 40 officers linked to 2023 boat capsize off Greece • Agency argues tribunal overturned sackings on technicalities; three-judge bench directs agency to fulfil requirements of due process ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Wednesday cleared the way for the Fe­­deral Investigation Agency (FIA) to reopen a departmental inquiry against officials allegedly linked to the fatal 2023 Greek migrant boat capsize tragedy. However, the court rejected the FIA’s appeal against an April 14 Federal Service Tribunal (FST) ruling, upholding the order to reinstate the dismissed FIA officers. A three-judge Supreme Court bench, headed by Justice Muhammad Ali Maz­har, took up appeals moved by the Dire­c­to­rate General Federal Investiga­tion Age­ncy (FIA) challenging the FST order. Pursuant to the Greece boat tragedy of 2023, FIA had penalised and dismissed 40 officers who were found to have allegedly facilitated the human smuggling of vulnerable individuals. Around 286 people departed from Libya, of whom 155 were killed when the boat capsized off the coast of Greece. Representing FIA, Deputy Attorney General Raja Shafqat Abbasi argued that the FST had set aside the dismissal orders merely on technical and procedural lapses, such as the non-compliance of procedure and a lack of opportunity for cross-examination. He argued that officers posted at the time at the Lahore, Karachi and Multan airports were under a statutory duty under their job descriptions to properly scrutinise tickets, passports, visas and the purpose of the visits to Libya, noting it was a war-torn country rather than a tourist destination. It was the duty of the officers to apply their minds as to why more than 286 persons were travelling to Libya from different airports of the country, Mr Abbasi said. The counsel submitted that there was at least gross omission and negligence, amounting to direct facilitation on the part of these officials, which enabled human smugglers to traffic innocent citizens from Pakistan to Libya and onward to Europe via a sea route. This led to the deaths of 155 Pakistanis and caused serious damage to the image of Pakistan internationally, he added. Mr Abbasi contended that if there was any procedural lapse in holding the departmental inquiry, the accused officials were not entitled to a “clean chit” of reinstatement in the job. At most, a fresh opportunity should be given to the FIA to conduct a de novo in­­quiry after providing a due opportunity for hearing and cross-examination, so that appropriate action may be taken aga­inst those found responsible in accor­da­nce with the law, the counsel contended. Concluding the hearing, the Supreme Court referred the matter to the FIA to initiate a fresh inquiry, if they deem it fit, in accordance with the law against the officials for whom evidence was on the record, after giving the officials an opportunity for a hearing. Published in Dawn, October 29th, 2026

items.title: Kayouh plaide pour une flotte marchande nationale forte et compétitive
items.description: L'Institut Supérieur d'Etudes Maritimes (ISEM) a lancé, mercredi à Casablanca, l'année académique 2026-2027, lors d'une cérémonie présidée par le ministre du Transport et de la Logistique, Abdessamad Kayouh. S'exprimant à cette occasion, le ministre a souligné que l'Institut a formé 48 promotions d'officiers, ainsi que des cadres exerçant au Maroc et à l'étranger, à bord des navires, dans les ports, l'industrie navale et les compagnies de transport et de logistique, notant que le rayonnement de l'ISEM s'étend au continent africain dans le cadre de la coopération Sud-Sud. Kayouh a indiqué que la vision du Roi Mohammed VI visant à faire de la façade atlantique un espace d'intégration économique place au cœur de ses priorités la constitution d'une flotte marchande nationale forte et compétitive, relevant que le ministère œuvre au développement d'un écosystème maritime intégré, où la flotte nationale constitue un levier de compétitivité, d'investissement et d’emploi. Ce chantier englobe le renforcement de la maintenance, de la réparation et de la transformation des navires, ainsi que l'extension progressive des capacités de construction navale, ouvrant de nouveaux débouchés aux jeunes, a poursuivi le responsable, précisant que son département vise à porter le nombre de lauréats de l'ISEM à 500 par an à l'horizon 2030, puis à 1.000 à l'horizon 2035. De son côté, le directeur de l'ISEM, Aissa Benazzouz, a fait savoir que l'Institut accueille 72 nouveaux étudiants issus des classes préparatoires, sélectionnés dès la première phase à l'issue d'épreuves orales, d'un examen médical et d'un test psychotechnique, notant que l'offre académique de cette année propose une nouvelle filière d'ingénieur en électrotechnique maritime, à laquelle s'ajouteront, en 2027-2028, un cycle d'ingénieur en architecture navale et une licence en hydrographie. Le cycle de doctorat démarre également cette année, faisant de l'ISEM un établissement de formation et de recherche, a-t-il ajouté, évoquant, par ailleurs, la modernisation de la gouvernance de l'Institut, le lancement d'un nouveau site web et la mise en place d'un système d'information pour la digitalisation des procédures académiques et administratives. La cérémonie a été marquée par la signature d'une convention avec l'Association des armateurs du Maroc (ARMA). Elle prévoit la participation de l'association aux instances de gouvernance de l'ISEM, la formation et l'encadrement des stages pratiques et des projets des étudiants des filières sciences navales et mécanique navale. Elle porte également sur la recherche de stages et l'insertion professionnelle des lauréats. Une deuxième convention a été conclue avec le Cluster Industrie Navale du Maroc (CINM). Elle vise l'accueil en stage et l'encadrement des projets de fin d'études des étudiants, notamment ceux du cycle d'ingénieur en construction et maintenance navales et en architecture navale. L'accord prévoit aussi l'intervention de professionnels du secteur dans les modules de formation, la réalisation de projets de recherche et développement d'intérêt commun et l'organisation conjointe d'événements scientifiques et techniques. Une troisième convention, signée entre l'ISEM, le CINM, l'ARMA et l'association Museemaritime.ma, définit le cadre de coopération pour la création d'un musée maritime au sein de l'Institut. The post Kayouh plaide pour une flotte marchande nationale forte et compétitive appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Drame ferroviaire en Espagne : Au moins 64 morts dans une collision entre deux trains à grande vitesse au sud de Madrid
items.description: Ce mercredi, l'Espagne a été frappée par une catastrophe ferroviaire majeure lorsqu'un train à grande vitesse de la compagnie nationale Renfe a percuté par l'arrière une rame de l'opérateur privé Iryo, immobilisée sur la ligne reliant Madrid à l'Andalousie près d'Urda (province de Tolède). L'accident, survenu vers 8h54 à environ 150 kilomètres au sud de la capitale, a fait au moins 64 morts et 179 blessés, dont 15 dans un état très grave. Alors que les équipes de secours ont lutté toute la matinée au milieu de scènes de chaos pour secourir les victimes, les premières investigations du centre de contrôle ferroviaire s'orientent vers une possible erreur humaine consécutive à une défaillance des systèmes de signalisation, déclenchant une vive controverse de la part des syndicats de cheminots. La terreur s'est abattue sur le réseau ferré espagnol. Sur un tronçon de la ligne à grande vitesse reliant Madrid au sud du pays, au niveau de la localité d'Urda dans la province de Tolède, un convoi AVE exploité par la compagnie publique Renfe est venu percuter par l'arrière un train de l'opérateur privé Iryo (filiale des chemins de fer italiens FS), qui s'était retrouvé immobilisé sur la voie. Le choc, survenu à une vitesse élevée, a été d'une brutalité extrême : plusieurs wagons ont été projetés hors des rails sous la force de l'impact. Au total, 477 passagers se trouvaient à bord des deux convois au moment de la collision. Sur le site du drame, les témoignages décrivent des visions d'horreur. Lors de l'impact, des voyageurs ont été violemment projetés dans les couloirs, tandis que des dizaines d'autres sont restés coincés sous les tôles broyées des wagons. Un incendie s'étant déclaré dans l'une des voitures, plusieurs passagers n'ont eu d'autre choix que de briser les vitres pour s'extirper en urgence par les fenêtres. Mobilisés en masse avec l'appui d'hélicoptères sanitaires et d'unités de soins intensifs, les services de secours ont œuvré sans relâche durant toute la matinée. Le bilan provisoire, particulièrement lourd, fait état d'au moins 64 morts et 179 blessés, dont 15 personnes luttant toujours contre la mort. Le Chef du gouvernement espagnol, Pedro Sánchez, s'est immédiatement rendu sur place pour exprimer la deuil de toute la nation. Comment deux rames à grande vitesse ont-elles pu se retrouver sur la même voie ? Les premiers éléments d'information recueillis au centre de contrôle ferroviaire à Madrid indiquent qu'une panne du système de signalisation de sécurité a d'abord perturbé la circulation sur la ligne. C'est à la suite de ce dysfonctionnement technique qu'un dispositif de signalisation de secours a été activé, conduisant à une reprise de circulation du train Renfe alors que la rame Iryo était toujours à l'arrêt sur le tronçon. Les enquêteurs privilégiant l'hypothèse d'une erreur humaine de régulation dans la gestion de cet incident. Cette mise en cause rapide suscite l'indignation des organisations représentatives des cheminots. Les syndicats ferroviaires ont fermement dénoncé la hâte avec laquelle la piste de l'erreur humaine a été avancée par la hiérarchie et le ministère. Ils exigent que les enquêtes judiciaires et techniques examinent rigoureusement l'état global du réseau, la maintenance des équipements de signalisation et les protocoles de dégradation de trafic. Cette tragédie ravive un traumatisme encore très frais dans le pays : elle intervient moins d'un an après l'accident d'Adamuz du 18 janvier dernier, qui avait coûté la vie à 46 personnes, soulevant une vive inquiétude sur la sécurité du réseau TGV espagnol. L’article Drame ferroviaire en Espagne : Au moins 64 morts dans une collision entre deux trains à grande vitesse au sud de Madrid est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Hegseth Fires a Top General
items.description: E arlier this week, the Pentagon’s chief planner, Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, was ousted from the Joint Chiefs of Staff. No explanation was given. This comes at an inopportune moment, given that President Trump may be planning to relaunch the war on Iran. Sylvia, the former commander of the 101st Airborne Division, becomes the latest in a long line of senior officers who have been shown the door since Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth arrived at the Pentagon almost two years ago. No replacement for Sylvia was named, and it is unclear who will take over his responsibilities. In the past, the deputy or vice director of the relevant directorate of the Joint Chiefs of Staff would fill the role on a temporary basis until the president nominated a candidate for Senate confirmation. Sylvia is the second person to be pushed out of the job of director of the Directorate for Strategy, Plans, and Policy at the Joint Chiefs of Staff, known inside the military as the J5, in the past year. His predecessor, Army Lieutenant General Joseph McGee, was forced to retire. “Now is not the time when you’d want to lose the J5,” a former Joint Chiefs of Staff official said. “This person would serve as a critical link between the operational force, the department policy, and the White House.” Sylvia’s departure presages more upheaval in the Pentagon’s upper echelons as Trump looks to break the stalemate with Iran and weighs renewed combat after Tuesday’s elections. Trump had considered striking Iran before the midterms, my colleagues and I previously reported , and U.S. Central Command, which is running the war effort, has prepared a variety of strike options. Those plans range from a short burst of strikes targeting Iran’s nuclear sites to a longer campaign aimed at pushing Iran’s economy closer to the brink—and Iran’s government to the negotiating table. But the president has not yet decided how to proceed, and any strikes are unlikely to happen before next week. The war, which began in February, has been relatively quiet in recent months as U.S. and Iranian forces face off in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global energy supplies. Iran effectively seized control of the strait shortly after the war began, while the U.S. has countered with a blockade of Iranian shipping. The webpage naming Sylvia as a member of the Joint Chiefs of Staff has already been taken down. Sylvia did not respond to a request for comment. I f the war has gotten bogged down, Hegseth’s campaign of firings at the Pentagon has not. Sylvia is at least the fifth general pushed out or fired this year, each holding key positions within the military. Hegseth forced out General Randy George, chief of staff of the Army, at the height of the U.S. strike campaign in Iran, despite the Army’s role in restocking key munitions, which are now in short supply. That same month, Hegseth removed General David Hodne, the head of the Army’s Transformation and Training Command, and ousted Major General William Green Jr., the head of the Army Chaplain Corps. And in June, Army General Chris “C.D.” Donahue stepped down as the head of U.S. Army Forces in Europe and Africa amid disagreements with Hegseth. Donahue was widely seen as one of the Army’s rising stars—a Delta Force leader who was considered a top candidate for Army chief of staff or even chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. In all, at least 26 admirals and generals have stepped down or been pushed out since Hegseth took control of the Pentagon less than two years ago. The Pentagon has rarely provided rationales, leaving those still in place to guess about the causes. The reasons, according to officials, tend to fall into one or more of three categories: previous work on policies that Hegseth considers “woke,” such as promoting diversity; perceived closeness to a former general considered persona non grata by the current administration, such as former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Mark Milley; and being suspected by Hegseth of leaking to the press. The message received through the ranks is that anyone viewed as insufficiently enthusiastic about Hegseth’s political views or priorities is at risk. Department of Defense officials told me that the rationale for firing Sylvia mirrored that of others pushed out before him: Hegseth lost confidence in him, and he did not get along with the top civilian in charge of policy, Elbridge Colby, the No. 3 leader at the Pentagon. In September, during his State of the Force speech, Hegseth said that the Pentagon had fired approximately 10 percent of its generals and admirals, and was eliminating another 10 percent of senior-officer positions. “The Chairman, the Joint Staff, and the Joint Force extend our deepest gratitude to Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia and his family for their 32 years of distinguished service to our nation,” a spokesperson for the Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a statement. “We wish him and his family the best as they graduate to new opportunities and the next chapters of their lives.” Last year, the conservative activist Laura Loomer called in a social-media post for the Trump administration to fire Sylvia’s son Gavin, an employee of the Department of Homeland Security as a data analyst at FEMA, charging that he had posted an inflammatory message on Instagram shortly after the assassination of Charlie Kirk. In the post, Loomer referred to the general as well, saying: “His father is a Major General in the United States Army and currently serves at the Pentagon. He was nominated for a third star by Joe Biden.” Her screed also took aim at Gavin Sylvia’s brother and grandmother. “These people hate us,” she wrote. “They don’t belong near the levers of our National Power.” She ended the post by saying Hegseth “should also review the employment of Gavin’s father, MG Brett Sylvia.” Gavin Sylvia was placed on administrative leave, The Washington Post reported . A 1994 graduate of the United States Military Academy, in West Point, Sylvia spent much of his career in the Army’s airborne and air-assault units. He commanded the 101st Airborne Division out of Fort Campbell, Kentucky. And he deployed multiple times to Iraq and Afghanistan as a member of the 101st. His military decorations include the Distinguished Service Medal, six Bronze Star Medals—including one with valor—and the Purple Heart. Missy Ryan and Marie-Rose Sheinerman contributed reporting.

items.title: Two deadly crashes this year raise concerns over Spain's rail security
items.description: Just nine months after a deadly railway accident near Adamuz in southern Spain, another high-speed train collision occurred on Wednesday on the same Madrid-Seville railway line, raising renewed concerns about the safety of Spain's high-speed rail network. The collision between two high-speed trains near Urda station in Toledo province, central Spain, has killed at least 68 people and injured 180 more. What happened and why? At around 8:54 a.m. local time (0754 GMT) on Wednesday, a Renfe-operated AVE train carrying 378 passengers struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train with 147 passengers aboard near Urda station. Both trains were heading from Madrid to Seville, according to Spain's Ministry of Transport and railway operator Renfe. At least 68 were killed, according to the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha. More than 180 people were reported injured, with some in critical condition. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday afternoon that the LZB train safety system had failed at around 8:30 a.m. due to a communication problem involving three computers, affecting a 63-km section of the railway and automatically bringing several trains to a halt. According to Puente, Adif's control center subsequently authorized the AVE train to resume normal operations at around 8:36 a.m., despite a red signal and the presence of the stationary Iryo train ahead. The AVE traveled approximately 25 km before crashing into the Iryo at around 8:53 a.m.. Under Spanish railway safety regulations, trains must remain stopped when the LZB system fails and the track ahead is occupied. Any authorized movement must follow restricted operating procedures requiring drivers to maintain a speed that allows them to stop upon detecting an obstacle ahead. Puente described the control center's decision as "inexplicable," while railway engineering expert Ramiro Aurin told Spanish news agency EFE that human error was the most likely explanation for the collision. However, the exact circumstances and responsibilities remain under investigation. Government response and public security The tragedy prompted the Spanish government and several major political parties to suspend their scheduled activities on Wednesday. During a visit to the accident site in Urda, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez stressed that rescuing victims and supporting their families remained the government's top priority. He pledged a thorough investigation into the collision, saying that any negligence or failures in railway safety systems would be addressed. "We will get to the bottom of this," Sanchez said. The government also declared three days of national mourning from October 29 to 31, while the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha activated an emergency response plan and mobilized additional rescue and medical resources. Several hospitals suspended scheduled activities to accommodate the injured, while psychological support teams were deployed to assist victims and their families. The accident also triggered calls for accountability. Opposition People's Party (PP) leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo said Spain had the right to know what was happening with its railway infrastructure. He called for immediate government and judicial investigations, as well as a comprehensive and independent review of the country's entire railway network. In Madrid, hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside the Ministry of Transport on Wednesday evening, demanding the resignation of Puente. Railway unions also called for stronger safety safeguards. The Independent Trade Union and Civil Servants' Central (CSIF) demanded an urgent explanation of the accident, accountability for those responsible, and greater investment in railway infrastructure and maintenance. The Spanish train drivers' union Semaf said it would proceed with a strike scheduled for Thursday, calling for stronger railway safety guarantees and structural reforms. The union also said it was considering further action following the latest tragedy. Growing concerns over rail safety The collision was Spain's second major fatal high-speed rail accident this year, with a crash near Adamuz, in the southern province of Cordoba, claiming 46 lives on January 18. While investigations into both accidents remain ongoing, experts have pointed to different possible causes. Jordi Vinolas Prat, a mechanical engineering professor at Francisco de Vitoria University, told Europa Press that the Adamuz disaster appeared to be linked to railway infrastructure problems, while the latest collision raised questions about signaling systems. Jose Trigueros, president of the Association of Civil Engineers, told Spanish national broadcaster RTVE that the latest collision was particularly concerning because high-speed rail safety systems were designed to prevent two trains from occupying the same section of track. He questioned the reliability of automated safety protections and the extent to which railway operations depended on human intervention. Concerns over railway safety had already been raised following the Adamuz disaster. Rafael Escudero, secretary-general of the Sindicato Ferroviario railway union, told Spanish radio station Onda Cero that the union had called for an audit of renovation works on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line after the January accident. He urged a review of how the more than 700 million euros ($770 million) allocated to upgrading the line had been spent, while stressing that the cause of Wednesday's collision remained under investigation. The latest tragedy has also unsettled some railway passengers. Daniel, a frequent traveler between Malaga and Madrid, told Spanish radio station Cadena SER that the accident had left him feeling angry and insecure, saying recent railway incidents had undermined his confidence in train travel. Civil engineer Martin Perea, a transport specialist and master's program director at Universidad Europea, also warned of serious damage to the reputation of Spain's railway system, calling for a thorough investigation, support for victims and their families, and a broader reassessment of the country's high-speed rail operations.

items.title: Bensaid Aït Idder : l'Alliance de la gauche dénonce des accusations visant la mémoire du résistant
items.description: L'Alliance de la gauche a condamné les propos attribués au vice-président du conseil communal de Tiflet, également membre du bureau politique d’un parti, qui aurait accusé le défunt résistant et dirigeant historique de l’Armée de libération, Mohamed Bensaid Aït Idder, de « collaboration » et de « trahison ». Dans un communiqué publié mercredi, le regroupement politique dénonce ce qu’il qualifie de « grave régression des droits » et d’atteinte à la mémoire collective des Marocains, ainsi qu’aux figures du mouvement de libération nationale et de la gauche marocaine. L'Alliance rappelle que Mohamed Bensaid Aït Idder a été l’une des figures de la résistance au colonialisme, ainsi que l’un des fondateurs et dirigeants de l’Armée de libération. Il souligne également son engagement en faveur de la liberté, de la dignité, de la démocratie, de la justice sociale et de l’égalité. Pour le regroupement, les accusations visant l’ancien militant ne relèvent pas d’une simple controverse politique, mais portent atteinte à la mémoire collective et aux sacrifices des générations qui ont combattu pour l’indépendance et les libertés. Elle estime que le parcours de Bensaid Aït Idder ne saurait être remis en cause par des déclarations qu’elle juge infondées. Le communiqué condamne également le fait que ces propos aient été tenus par un élu au sein d’une institution communale. L'Alliance de la gauche tient le président du conseil communal ainsi que les autorités de tutelle pour responsables de leur silence face à ce qu’il considère comme une atteinte à l’histoire nationale. Le regroupement demande à l’auteur des déclarations de les retirer immédiatement et de présenter des excuses publiques au peuple marocain, à la famille du défunt ainsi qu’à ses compagnons de lutte. Par ailleurs, la formation dénonce ce qu’elle présente comme une tentative de réhabilitation de responsables « tortionnaires » accusés d’avoir pratiqué la torture contre des militants durant les années de plomb. Elle en appelle ainsi aux institutions concernées pour mettre effectivement en œuvre les recommandations de l’Instance équité et réconciliation (IER), notamment en matière de lutte contre l’impunité, de garanties de non-répétition, de préservation de la mémoire nationale et de réparation des préjudices individuels, collectifs et territoriaux. Le regroupement affirme enfin sa volonté de rester fidèle aux valeurs défendues par Mohamed Bensaid Aït Idder, en réaffirmant son attachement à la liberté, à la dignité, à la démocratie, à la justice sociale, à l’égalité et à l’éthique de l’action politique. items.title: Why Wouldn’t Google Tell Me Who Won the 2020 Election?
items.description: For anyone who isn’t angling for a job in the Trump administration, “Who won the 2020 presidential election?” should be an easy question. But when I asked Google’s AI Mode—the AI function built into its search bar—about the race earlier today, the bot clammed up. “For official results and data regarding the 2020 United States presidential election, including the certified breakdown of electoral and popular votes by candidate, you can review the certified reports published by the Federal Election Commission (FEC),” it said. That was it. No links, no citations, nothing else except the standard fine-print disclaimer that AI can make mistakes. Yesterday, users of the social network Bluesky circulated screenshots of Google’s AI tool refusing to declare Joe Biden the 2020 victor, even as it readily named Donald Trump the winner of the 2016 and 2024 elections. By this morning, it had become a meme of sorts, as users shared their own twists on the query and came up with funny ways to trick the bot into spilling the truth. Asking Google’s AI to spell the winner’s name backwards, for instance, appeared to unlock the correct answer: “ nebiB eoJ won the 2020 United States presidential election,” the bot said . When one user responded to Google’s nonanswer with “what the hell,” the AI coughed up the true result and apologized for initially refusing to name Biden. AI tools giving strange answers is nothing new. (When Google launched its AI-powered search summaries in 2024, some users were told that the best way to add cheese to pizza was by using glue .) Still, for today’s bots to flub such a simple yet consequential factual question is not normal. In my tests, ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft’s Copilot, X’s Grok, and even the Trump administration’s own America.gov chatbot all correctly said that Biden won the 2020 election. As Americans begin to get more of their election information from AI , it’s disquieting to see perhaps the world’s most influential AI information source fail to do so. The issue wasn’t confined to AI Mode, which turns Google Search into a full chatbot. A standard Google search for who won the 2020 presidential election also failed to trigger an AI summary at the top of the page, and the search engine surfaced only links to other websites. (A question about the 2016 presidential election did trigger an AI answer.) Google now offers such AI overviews in response to a majority of queries, though not ones for which it lacks access to authoritative sources. People have suspected something nefarious in the omission, and it’s easy to see why. Trump still claims that he won the 2020 election, and questions about the result have reportedly become a litmus test of loyalty to the president. It doesn’t help that Google has a recent history of tweaking its products to comport with his preferences. At the start of Trump’s presidency, he issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America,” and Google changed the name on Google Maps. It did the same in August with Lake Ontario, changing its name to “Lake America.” At a rally last week, Trump said he had recently called Google CEO Sundar Pichai to see whether he would rename the Atlantic Ocean too. (Trump said Pichai pushed back on that one.) In this case, there’s no evidence that Google intentionally censored its chatbot. When I first asked Google about the bizarre result this morning, the company said it was looking into the issue. By this afternoon, Google said that it had identified the problem and was working to fix it. “Our systems verify election responses using news articles or AP data for recent elections, and historic records for older ones,” the company said on X. “There was a technical gap with 2020—same is true for 2022 Senate races, which we’re also working to fix.” Google noted that its stand-alone Gemini chatbot didn’t have the same problem as its AI-search tool, though it didn’t say why. A spokesperson for the company declined to answer further questions. When I tried the same search later in the day, Google’s AI quickly named Biden as the 2020 winner. Let’s take Google at its word that this was unintentional. Large language models are opaque and unpredictable by nature. Complicating matters, the big AI firms have trained their chatbots to be careful around certain sensitive topics, including election results, and those guardrails can sometimes manifest in unexpected ways. How reassured should we be? Well, it’s good to know that Google hasn’t made election denial an official company policy and secretly embedded it in search results. Crazy as that might sound, we have to look only at Elon Musk’s xAI for an example of a tech company seemingly manipulating its chatbot’s answers to reflect its owner’s politics. Last year, Grok started injecting claims about a “white genocide” in South Africa into answers about unrelated topics. (The company blamed an “unauthorized modification” to the bot’s code.) Still, Google’s suggestion that this was just an unfortunate mix-up raises a different set of concerns. Google says its AI overviews reach more than 2 billion people a month. If the company’s search bots trip over the most elementary of election questions, what does that say about all of the subtler ways they could go wrong? Victoria Feng contributed reporting.

items.title: UN votes overwhelmingly against US embargo on Cuba
items.description: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday adopted a resolution calling for an end to the decades-old US embargo on Cuba. The resolution was adopted with 130 votes in favor, 17 against and 25 abstentions. It expresses concern about the continued promulgation and application of laws and regulations, including the Helms-Burton Act enacted by the United States in 1996, whose extraterritorial effects undermine the sovereignty of other states, the legitimate interests of individuals and entities under their jurisdiction, and the freedom of trade and navigation. The resolution calls on all states to refrain from promulgating and applying such laws and measures, and urges states that have applied and continue to apply such laws and measures to take necessary steps to repeal or invalidate them as soon as possible. Wednesday's resolution marked the 34th consecutive adoption of a resolution on the necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States on Cuba. Cuba celebrated the overwhelming approval of the resolution, calling it a "victory" in the face of unprecedented pressure from Washington to defeat the initiative. In a post on X, Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel described the resolution's broad backing as a "victory for the heroic Cuban people," who have not surrendered despite the "economic suffocation, threats and abuse by the US government." The outcome "is a triumph of the truth over those who rely on lies and blackmail to subject an entire nation to collective punishment," he said. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez, who led the Cuban delegation to the UN General Assembly, also called the vote a "new victory" against the US sanctions and further proof that "Cuba is not a threat, the embargo is." For more than six decades, Washington has imposed stiff economic, commercial and financial sanctions on Cuba, a policy intensified by the Trump administration. Official Cuban government figures show the US embargo has caused nearly $179 billion in economic losses to the Caribbean island. (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: Indonesia: Landmark Ruling Allows Civilian Trials of Soldiers
items.description: Click to expand Image The Constitutional Court of Indonesia, in Jakarta, October 2023. © 2023 Yasuyoshi Chiba/AFP via Getty Images (London) – The Indonesian Constitutional Court’s ruling requiring reform of the military justice system so that military personnel accused of ordinary crimes can be tried in civilian courts is a major step for justice in Indonesia, Human Rights Watch said today. The government should immediately revise the 1997 Military Justice Law, which has long prevented civilian prosecutions of members of the armed forces for crimes under the Indonesian criminal code, including for serious human rights violations. On October 15, 2026, the Constitutional Court’s nine justices unanimously ruled that the Military Justice Law is conditionally unconstitutional under articles 24(1) and 28D(1) of the 1945 Constitution, which guarantee an independent judiciary and equality before the law. The law will become unconstitutional if it is not amended by October 2028, giving the government a two-year deadline. “The Constitutional Court’s landmark ruling recognizes that Indonesia’s military courts aren’t capable of impartially trying crimes against civilians, as victims and human rights defenders have said for decades, ” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “President Prabowo Subianto and the Indonesian parliament should consult with victims and rights groups and promptly amend the military justice law.” Under the 1997 law, civilian police cannot investigate military personnel, with only a few rarely invoked exceptions. Even when soldiers serving in civilian institutions have been accused of crimes under the criminal code, military courts have had jurisdiction over the case. Human Rights Watch found that Indonesia’s military justice system lacks transparency, independence, and impartiality, and has failed to properly investigate and prosecute alleged serious human rights abuses by military personnel. The petitioners challenged articles 9(1), 43(3), and 127 of the law, which allow active duty military personnel to be tried in military courts even for crimes ordinarily prosecuted in civilian courts. The Constitutional Court found that the distinction between military offenses and ordinary criminal offenses must be clearly defined. Justice Enny Nurbaningsih said that when an offense has no military character but accountability for it remains within a command-based system, “there is a structural risk that military’s institutional interests will conflict with the need to ensure independent and impartial legal proceedings.” The Constitutional Court also noted that the military judiciary is not fully integrated into the judicial system overseen by the Supreme Court and urged lawmakers to create a single system. Military judges are active duty soldiers, and investigation, prosecution, and adjudication all take place within the military chain-of-command. Revisions to the Military Justice Law have been pending for decades. As part of structural reforms that followed the end of authoritarian rule under President Soeharto from 1965 to 1998, the 2004 Armed Forces Law made soldiers subject to civilian courts for ordinary crimes. However, that provision would only take effect when a new military justice law was enacted. The Constitutional Court’s ruling imposes a two-year time frame for those revisions, which successive Indonesian governments have deferred. Muhammad Afif Abdul Qoyim, a lawyer from the Indonesian Legal Aid Foundation, told Human Rights Watch: “There is no need to wait two years to revise the Law on Military Justice so that new rules are in line with the Constitutional Court’s ruling.” Serious abuses by Indonesian security forces have gone unpunished for decades because of legal restrictions on civilian investigations and prosecutions under the 1997 law, Human Rights Watch said. On March 12, 2026, military personnel carried out an acid attack against Andrie Yunus, a 27-year-old deputy coordinator at KontraS (Commission for the Disappeared and Victims of Violence), causing burns over 24 percent of his body and possible loss of sight in his right eye. A military court in Jakarta convicted four soldiers in June and sentenced them to 18 months to three years in prison and dismissal from the military. On August 20, a military appeals court reduced the two longest sentences by six months each and overturned their dishonorable discharges. The Judicial Commission has alleged ethical violations by the panel that tried the case at first instance. KontraS said in a statement that the Constitutional Court ruling “closes a legal loophole that has been seen as shielding errant soldiers from accountable law enforcement, and marks a new chapter in upholding the rule of law and completing the mandate of security sector reform in Indonesia.” One of the petitioners in the case is the mother of a 15-year-old boy tortured to death in Medan, North Sumatra, in 2024 by a soldier who was sentenced by a military court to only 10 months in prison, though the maximum penalty is 15 years. In Papua, the military justice system has repeatedly failed victims of violence allegedly committed by military personnel. Under President Prabowo Subianto, a former general dismissed from the military for human rights violations, the military’s role in civilian affairs has expanded. In March 2025, the national legislature passed amendments to the Armed Forces Law to allow active duty officers to hold more government posts. The number of civilian institutions open to serving soldiers—which includes the Supreme Court and the Attorney General’s office—rose from 10 to 14. Lawmakers should prioritize amending the Military Justice Law through an open process with meaningful participation of victims and civil society, Human Rights Watch said. The amended law should clarify investigative and prosecutorial powers and provide a mechanism for transferring cases from military courts to the civilian system. “Justice for civilian victims of military abuses shouldn’t be blocked by an unfair military court system,” Pearson said. “Amending the law on military justice will support efforts begun decades ago to ensure the Indonesian military is a professional, credible institution whose soldiers are held accountable when they commit serious abuses.”

items.title: Niger: Prominent Journalist ‘Disappeared’ for 2 Months
items.description: Click to expand Image Nigerien journalist Moussa Kaka, former correspondent for Radio France Internationale, February 12, 2007. © 2007 Seyllou/AFP via Getty Images (Nairobi) – Niger’s authorities should urgently disclose the whereabouts of the prominent journalist Moussa Kaka, who was forcibly disappeared two months ago, Human Rights Watch said today. They should ensure his safety and release him unless he has been charged with a valid criminal offense. On August 31, 2026, Kaka, the director-general of Radio Télévision Saraounia and a former correspondent for Radio France Internationale (RFI), left his office in Niamey, the capital, to return home but never arrived, raising immediate concerns. For weeks, his family and colleagues were not able to obtain information about his whereabouts. On September 25, during Niger’s Universal Periodic Review at the United Nations in Geneva, Justice Minister Alio Daouda acknowledged that Kaka was being detained. The minister said Kaka was being held for an alleged “offense” and would “answer before the courts,” but provided no details about the accusation or his place of detention. “Two months after Moussa Kaka vanished in Niger, the authorities have yet to provide his location or explain his detention,” said Ilaria Allegrozzi, senior Sahel researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Kaka’s family will continue to grapple with the uncertainty until the authorities resolve his disappearance.” Kaka is a respected figure in African investigative journalism. For years, he reported for RFI in Niger, until the military junta suspended its broadcasts in 2023. Throughout his career, he has continued his work under successive governments despite the risks and repeated detentions for his journalism. In September 2007, under then-President Mamadou Tandja, the authorities arrested Kaka and accused him of links to ethnic Tuareg rebels, following his extended coverage of the Tuareg rebellion in northern Niger. He spent 379 days in prison before being released in October 2008 following a sustained national and international campaign for his freedom. In October 2025, police in Niamey arrested Kaka along with five other journalists after they announced on social media a press briefing about a government-created solidarity fund intended to support the country’s security forces. The journalists were charged with “complicity in distributing documents likely to disturb public order” under Niger’s broad cybercrime law. All six were subsequently released. Kaka’s recent forced disappearance came amid heightened political tensions following an attempted military coup in Niamey on August 29. After mutinous soldiers attempted to seize power, the junta arrested dozens of suspected soldiers and a former minister. Russian government-controlled Africa Corps forces were called upon to help suppress the mutiny. Kaka’s colleagues and friends have expressed concern that his disappearance may be linked to the junta’s crackdown after the attempted coup. Reporters Without Borders has referred Kaka’s case to the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances, following an earlier referral to the African Union’s special rapporteur on freedom of expression and access to information. African civil society organizations raised his case at the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights in mid-October in Dakar, Senegal. Journalists and human rights activists across Africa have also called for his release. “Moussa Kaka’s place is not in detention,” said Alioune Tine, a prominent Senegalese human rights defender and former UN rights expert. “His detention is absolutely unjustified and violates Niger’s international human rights obligations, including provisions of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, which Niger has signed and ratified.” Kaka’s case highlights growing concerns about media freedom and political repression in Niger, Human Rights Watch said. Since seizing power in a 2023 coup, Niger’s military junta has solidified its rule, dismantled democratic institutions, and intensified repression of dissidents. They have dissolved political parties, suspended dozens of civil society organizations, detained journalists under a broad cybercrime law, stripped exiled political opponents of their nationality, announced the country’s withdrawal from the International Criminal Court, and extended the political transition without holding elections. The authorities also continue to arbitrarily detain former President Mohamed Bazoum and his wife, and a prominent human rights defender, Moussa Tiangari. Under international human rights law, an enforced disappearance occurs when state agents, or people acting with the state’s authorization, support, or acquiescence, deprive someone of their liberty and then refuse to acknowledge the detention or conceal the person’s fate or whereabouts. Enforced disappearance places victims at heightened risk of torture and extrajudicial execution. It also inflicts profound suffering on families, who are left uncertain whether their loved ones are alive or dead and denied access to justice. “Niger’s authorities should immediately account for Kaka and free him if he hasn’t been fairly charged,” Allegrozzi said. “Governments and international organizations should press the junta to take immediate action in Kaka’s case.”

items.title: Trump Is Closing From Behind
items.description: M odern political history offers few examples of closing arguments that appear more out of touch, self-defeating, or downright bizarre than what Donald Trump has offered his fellow Republicans ahead of next week’s midterm elections. In 1980, when Ronald Reagan told voters to consider Jimmy Carter’s presidency and ask themselves, “Are you better off than you were four years ago?,” it helped turn a tight race into a Reagan landslide. But many stretch-run messages prove deeply ineffective and are quickly forgotten. Ahead of the 1998 midterms, Republicans went all in on investigations that led to the impeachment of President Bill Clinton only to be rebuked by voters. President Obama’s insistence in 2010 that the country was coming out of the financial crisis led to his party enduring a “shellacking.” And during the 2018 midterms, Trump and his fellow Republicans tried to stoke fears about an alleged caravan of migrants headed toward the United States, only to have skeptical voters hand the House of Representatives to Democrats. This time around, Trump’s primary rationale for why voters should support the GOP, as best I can tell, is that the affordability crisis is a “hoax,” Bill Maher is a “loser,” and Senator Jon Husted of Ohio has a nice physique. That easy-to-mock message has been accompanied by a staggering number of missteps. Just for starters, he’s belittled the impact of his stalled war with Iran, sided with Russia as it continues to pummel Ukrainian cities, defended an attack ad from the GOP candidate for Ohio governor that repulsed other top Republicans, downplayed high energy prices while boasting that U.S. oil and gas companies are “making a freaking fortune,” embraced AI as the nation turns against it, obsessed over White House construction projects, and spent a lot of time talking about handsome men, Husted being just one. Many Republicans, and even some in Trump’s orbit, don’t quite get it. What has happened, they ask, to the instincts of the man who authored two of the most improbable victories in American political history? Trump’s superpower was his intuitive understanding of what motivated his supporters. Many Republicans privately tell me that he’s lost that feel. Trump now lives, they think, in a gilded bubble, palling around with billionaires, oblivious to—and, even worse, uncaring about—the problems facing so many voters. His approval rating has slipped to the low 30s. He’s become so toxic that some Republicans in tight races don’t want him anywhere near their state or congressional district, believing his rallies will harm more than help. Strategists in both parties expect Democrats to take control of the House, while the Senate is a true toss-up —a stunning reversal from the beginning of the year, when the upper chamber’s map looked so favorable for Republicans, and Trump cut a dominant figure. Suddenly, Republicans find themselves fighting to keep Senate seats in deep-red states: Kansas. Alaska. South Carolina. Ohio. Iowa. Mississippi. Texas. Trump is campaigning across the country, imploring his supporters to turn out for him one last time. But he’s given Republicans next to nothing to run on, and polls show that voters believe his economic policies are failing, his deportation program has gone too far, and his war is misguided. He instead has leaned hard on the political battles of the past, reheating fears about transgender surgeries (from his 2024 campaign), Muslim terrorists (all the way back to 2016), and even communism. (The guy does have a fondness for the ’80s .) For good measure, Trump’s Department of Justice charged the former FBI Director James Comey for a third time—the first two didn’t stick—because nothing screams being in tune with the everyday concerns of voters than trying to revive a faltering retribution campaign against a political foe your administration once targeted over a photograph of seashells. One Republican up for reelection who would speak with me only on the condition of anonymity, so as not to alienate the president, put it succinctly: “We may have lost the plot here.” N ot that long ago, the president was tossing Trump 2028 hats around, and Democrats were freaking out that he might be powerful enough to defy the Constitution. But that headgear now seems dated, as does the apparel line trumpeting that Trump Was Right About Everything! Many Republicans tell me that their party’s biggest problem just days from the election is that voters feel like Trump hasn’t kept his core promises. End foreign wars? Nope, there’s a new one in Iran that’s sent gas prices up and depleted the U.S. munitions supply. Plus, Trump has appeared to side with Russia over Ukraine in a conflict he once promised to end in 24 hours. Bring prices down? Well, the war in the Middle East has made that impossible, as have Trump’s haphazard trade wars, including tariffs on once-friendly trading partners such as Canada and the European Union. And while many Americans are struggling, Trump and his family are growing exponentially wealthier. Deport the worst of the worst? Trump’s massive roundups are targeting not just violent criminals or gang members, but also longtime community members, neighbors, parishioners, teammates, and friends with no criminal records. Many Americans have been horrified by the violence unleashed by masked federal agents, especially the killing of two U.S. citizens in the streets of Minneapolis. [ Read: Trump’s gamble to end the Iran war ] That Trump wants to focus on anything other than these broken promises while out on the campaign trail is perhaps unsurprising. At his Monday rally in Corinth, Mississippi, he spent seven minutes—nearly 10 percent of his entire speech—discussing his efforts to redecorate the White House. The day before—when Trump traveled to a rally in Port Huron, Michigan—the president’s talking points included faulting President Biden for the war in Ukraine; falsely claiming that more oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz than before the war; deeming Norway a “shithouse country”; calling Abdul El-Sayed, the state’s Democratic nominee for Senate, a jihadist (five times); saying that, should he win, El-Sayed will be the only senator who must go through a metal detector to get to work; comparing a vote against El-Sayed to stopping a deadly terror attack; asking the Trinidadian rapper Nicki Minaj to stand before thousands of his supporters so that they could appreciate her butt; and lauding the boulder-like shoulders, thick fingers, massive feet, and firm backside of (who else?) Husted, his preferred candidate for Senate in a different state. Over the course of that day, he spent three and a half minutes talking about Husted’s football career, which is three and a half minutes more than he talked about the lawmaker’s policies. Rather than dispel the notion that he has lost sight of what actually matters to voters, Trump on Sunday night released a social-media screed of more than 1,300 words (his longest Truth Social post ever) that assailed Maher for being ungrateful after the president hosted the comedian and talk-show host at the White House for dinner. The president has also fumed that Obama said over the weekend that Trump’s new White House decor is “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Trump angrily complained about the dig multiple times just yesterday. [ Read: Leave the Cheesecake Factory out of this ] Trump has also found himself on the wrong side of the day’s top issues. He misses few chances to mock the affordability crisis. Republicans and Democrats alike have swiftly turned on artificial intelligence, blasting the industry’s data centers as loud and expensive, and warning voters that the rapidly developing technology could take away their jobs or even their lives . Yet Trump has refused to regulate AI, knowing that the industry is propping up the stock market. His only nod toward change is trying to rename it “Super Intelligence.” Last week, Trump loudly supported a controversial ad from the campaign of Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for Ohio governor. The video features the estranged mother of the Democratic nominee Amy Acton, Donna Arthur, who accuses her daughter of lying about her past. It doesn’t mention that the two women have not spoken for decades, after the candidate’s stepfather was indicted for molesting her. The backlash was fierce and bipartisan; the state’s current Republican governor, Mike DeWine, denounced the ad and demanded that it be pulled. Trump not only supported it but also urged Ramaswamy to “say thank you, God, very much” for such political good fortune. Divine intervention or not, several GOP strategists believe the ad could doom Ramaswamy. Some GOP candidates in tight races—Susan Collins in Maine, John Sununu in New Hampshire—have sent word to the White House that Trump isn’t welcome to campaign alongside them. The president has instead been dispatched to deep-red states with the hopes of turning out enough of his die-hard supporters to avoid losing once-safe Senate seats. Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, insisted to me in a statement that Trump is remaining focused while “crisscrossing the country with unmatched energy and enthusiasm to deliver a simple message: with Republicans in control of Congress, Americans can expect safer streets, lower taxes, a secure border, and energy dominance.” T he most eyebrow-raising October surprise has been Trump’s unfiltered and rather randy assessments of the male form . His motivations remain a mystery, but some in the president’s circle have theories. One outside adviser who is close to the president told me that it began when Trump, while rallying for Husted two weeks ago, was first told that the senator had played college football in the late ’80s. Trump was impressed and began publicly ruminating over the next few days about Husted’s physique, including declaring that the senator’s “ass is like a pile of muscle.” That admiration quickly became a subject of interest on social media and cable shows, some of which resurfaced clips of Trump praising the good looks of Secret Service agents, generals, and a quarterback for the New York Giants. All of that prompted amused chatter about the 80-year-old president. But Trump has always been keenly interested in appearances, female or male, and has long made hiring decisions based on wanting looks out of “central casting.” As that adviser noted to me, Trump has spent decades in the public eye, obsessing about how his tan or hair looked on television; he’s given a lot of thought to his own appearance, so it’s not surprising that he’d think about how others look, too. [ Read: A different kind of fading president ] What is more surprising to many around Trump is just how freely he is expressing those thoughts. Any filter appears to be long gone. Then again, there may be simpler explanations: Once the Husted comments went viral, Trump’s rally crowds have come to expect the lines and have begun to laugh along, reinforcing the president’s sense that the material is working. And Trump would rather discuss almost anything besides the price of gas—even Husted’s posterior. Jack Rodriquez-Vars contributed research to this report.
